3.2.s:
.. śrīgaṇeśāya namaḥ.....
tartuṃ saṃhṛtivāridhiṃ trijagatāṃ naurnāma yasya prabhoryenedaṃ sakalaṃ vibhāti satataṃ jātaṃ sthitaṃ saṃsṛtam..
yaścaitanyaghanapramāṇa vidhuro vedāṃtavedyo vibhustaṃ vande sahajaprakāśamamalaṃ śrīrāmacandraṃ param ( ..1.. )
3.2.d:
.. श्रीगणेशाय नमः.....
तर्तुं संहृतिवारिधिं त्रिजगतां नौर्नाम यस्य प्रभोर्येनेदं सकलं विभाति सततं जातं स्थितं संसृतम्..
यश्चैतन्यघनप्रमाण विधुरो वेदांतवेद्यो विभुस्तं वन्दे सहजप्रकाशममलं श्रीरामचन्द्रं परम् ( ..1.. )
3.2.m:
Homage to glorious Gaṇeśa.
Whose name is a boat for the three worlds to cross the ocean of dissolution, the Lord / through whom all this, born, maintained, and transmuted, shines continuously,
who is a mass of consciousness, beyond means of knowledge, knowable through Vedānta, the all-pervading Lord— / to that supreme, pure, self-luminous Śrī Rāmacandra I bow. (1)

3.2.s:
dārāḥ putrā dhanaṃ vā parijanasahito baṃdhuvargaḥ priyo vā mātā bhrātā pitā vā śvaśurakulajanā bhṛtyaaiśvaryyavitte..
vidyā rūpaṃ vimalabhavanaṃ yauvanaṃ yauvataṃ vā sarve vyarthaṃ maraṇasamaye dharma ekaḥ sahāyaḥ (..2..)
naimiṣe nimiṣakṣetre ṛṣayaḥ śaunakādayaḥ..
satraṃ svargāya lokāya sahasrasamamāsata .. 1 ..
ekadā sūtamāyāṃtaṃ dṛṣṭvā taṃ śaunakādayaḥ ..
paraṃ harṣaṃ samāviṣṭāḥ papurnetraiḥ sucetasā..
citrāḥ śrotuṃ kathāstatra parivavrustapasvinaḥ .. 2..
3.2.d:
दाराः पुत्रा धनं वा परिजनसहितो बंधुवर्गः प्रियो वा माता भ्राता पिता वा श्वशुरकुलजना भृत्यऐश्वर्य्यवित्ते..
विद्या रूपं विमलभवनं यौवनं यौवतं वा सर्वे व्यर्थं मरणसमये धर्म एकः सहायः (..2..)
नैमिषे निमिषक्षेत्रे ऋषयः शौनकादयः..
सत्रं स्वर्गाय लोकाय सहस्रसममासत .. 1 ..
एकदा सूतमायांतं दृष्ट्वा तं शौनकादयः ..
परं हर्षं समाविष्टाः पपुर्नेत्रैः सुचेतसा..
चित्राः श्रोतुं कथास्तत्र परिवव्रुस्तपस्विनः .. 2..
3.2.m:
Wives, sons, or wealth, or one's beloved circle of kinsmen together with attendants, / mother, brother, father, or in-laws, servants, power, and property,
learning, beauty, a spotless mansion, youth, or young women— / all is useless at the hour of death; dharma alone is one's companion. (2)
In Naimiṣa, the sacred field of Nimiṣa, the seers headed by Śaunaka / celebrated a sacrificial session lasting a thousand years to attain the heavenly realm. (1)
Once, seeing Sūta arriving, Śaunaka and the others, / overcome with supreme joy, drank him in with their eyes and happy minds; / the ascetics gathered around there to hear wondrous tales. (2)

3.2.s:
atha teṣūpaviṣṭeṣu tapasviṣu mahātmasu..
nirdiṣṭamāsanaṃ bheje vinayāllomaharṣaṇiḥ ..3..
3.2.d:
अथ तेषूपविष्टेषु तपस्विषु महात्मसु..
निर्दिष्टमासनं भेजे विनयाल्लोमहर्षणिः ..3..
3.2.m: Then, when those great-souled ascetics were seated, / the son of Romaharṣaṇa modestly took the appointed seat.

3.2.s:
sukhāsīnaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā vighnāṃtamupalakṣya ca ..
athāpṛcchaṃsta ṛṣayaḥ kāścitprāstāvikīḥ kathāḥ .. 4 ..
3.2.d:
सुखासीनं च तं दृष्ट्वा विघ्नांतमुपलक्ष्य च ..
अथापृच्छंस्त ऋषयः काश्चित्प्रास्ताविकीः कथाः .. 4 ..
3.2.m: Seeing him comfortably seated and noting that obstacles had ceased, / those seers then asked about certain contextual stories:

3.2.s:
purāṇamakhilaṃ tāta purā te'dhītavānpitā ..
kaccittvayāpi tatsarvamadhītaṃ lomaharṣaṇe.. 5..
3.2.d:
पुराणमखिलं तात पुरा तेऽधीतवान्पिता ..
कच्चित्त्वयापि तत्सर्वमधीतं लोमहर्षणे.. 5..
3.2.m: “Dear one, formerly your father studied the entire Purāṇa. / Have you also studied all of that, O Lomaharṣaṇa?

3.2.s:
kathayasva kathāṃ sūta puṇyāṃ pāpaniṣūdinīm..
śrutvā yāṃ yāti vilayaṃ pāpaṃ janmaśatodbhavam .. 6 ..
3.2.d:
कथयस्व कथां सूत पुण्यां पापनिषूदिनीम्..
श्रुत्वा यां याति विलयं पापं जन्मशतोद्भवम् .. 6 ..
3.2.m: Tell us, O Sūta, a sacred tale that destroys sin, / hearing which, sin born of a hundred lifetimes goes to dissolution.”

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
śrībhāratyaṃghriyugalaṃ gaṇanāthapadadvayam ..
sarveṣāṃ caiva devānāṃ namaskṛtya vadāmyaham .. 7..
3.2.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
श्रीभारत्यंघ्रियुगलं गणनाथपदद्वयम् ..
सर्वेषां चैव देवानां नमस्कृत्य वदाम्यहम् .. 7..
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Bowing to the pair of feet of the venerable Sarasvatī and the two feet of Gaṇanātha, / and to all the gods, I shall speak.

3.2.s:
śaktīṃścaiva vasūṃścaiva grahānyajñādidevatāḥ ..
namaskṛtya śubhānviprānkavimukhyāṃśca sarvaśaḥ ..8..
3.2.d:
शक्तींश्चैव वसूंश्चैव ग्रहान्यज्ञादिदेवताः ..
नमस्कृत्य शुभान्विप्रान्कविमुख्यांश्च सर्वशः ..8..
3.2.m: Bowing to the Śaktis, the Vasus, the planets, the deities of sacrifice and the rest, / to the auspicious brahmins and the foremost of poets everywhere,

3.2.s:
abhīṣṭadevatāścaiva praṇamya gurusattamam ..
namaskṛtya śubhāndevānrāmādīṃśca viśeṣataḥ ..9..|
3.2.d:
अभीष्टदेवताश्चैव प्रणम्य गुरुसत्तमम् ..
नमस्कृत्य शुभान्देवान्रामादींश्च विशेषतः ..9..|
3.2.m: and bowing to the chosen deities and to the best of gurus, / bowing to the auspicious gods, especially Rāma and others,

3.2.s:
yānsmṛtvā vividhaiḥ pāpairmucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ..
teṣāṃ prasādādvakṣye'haṃ tīrthānāṃ phalamuttamam ..
sarveṣāṃ ca niyaṃtāraṃ dharmātmānaṃ praṇamya ca .. 3.2.1.10 ..
3.2.d:
यान्स्मृत्वा विविधैः पापैर्मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ..
तेषां प्रसादाद्वक्ष्येऽहं तीर्थानां फलमुत्तमम् ..
सर्वेषां च नियंतारं धर्मात्मानं प्रणम्य च .. 3.2.1.10 ..
3.2.m: remembering whom one is freed from diverse sins, without doubt— / by their grace, and having bowed to the virtuous controller of all, / I shall proclaim the supreme fruit of the sacred fords.

3.2.s:
dharmmāraṇyapatistriviṣṭapapatirnityaṃ bhavānīpatiḥ pāpādvaḥ sthirabhogayogasulabho devaḥ sa dharmeśvaraḥ ..
sarveṣāṃ hṛdayāni jīvakalayā vyāpya sthitaḥ sarvadā dhyātvā yaṃ na punarviśaṃti manujāḥ saṃsārakārāgṛham.. 11 ..
3.2.d:
धर्म्मारण्यपतिस्त्रिविष्टपपतिर्नित्यं भवानीपतिः पापाद्वः स्थिरभोगयोगसुलभो देवः स धर्मेश्वरः ..
सर्वेषां हृदयानि जीवकलया व्याप्य स्थितः सर्वदा ध्यात्वा यं न पुनर्विशंति मनुजाः संसारकारागृहम्.. 11 ..
3.2.m: May the Lord of Dharmāraṇya, the Lord of Heaven, the eternal Lord of Bhavānī, that god Dharmeśvara, easily attained through yoga and steadfast enjoyment, [protect] you from sin! / Pervading the hearts of all as the particle of the individual soul, He abides forever; meditating on Him, mortals do not enter the prison-house of saṃsāra again.

3.2.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
ekadā tu sa dharmmo vai jagāma brahmasaṃsadi ..
tāṃ sabhāṃ sa samālokya jñānaniṣṭho'bhavattadā.. 12 ..
3.2.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एकदा तु स धर्म्मो वै जगाम ब्रह्मसंसदि ..
तां सभां स समालोक्य ज्ञाननिष्ठोऽभवत्तदा.. 12 ..
3.2.m: Sūta said: / Once, indeed, Dharma went to the assembly of Brahmā. / Beholding that assembly, he then became absorbed in knowledge.

3.2.s:
devairmunivaraiḥ krāṃtāṃ sabhāmālokya vismitaḥ ..
devairyakṣaistathā nāgaiḥ pannagaiśca tathā'suraiḥ. .. 13..
3.2.d:
देवैर्मुनिवरैः क्रांतां सभामालोक्य विस्मितः ..
देवैर्यक्षैस्तथा नागैः पन्नगैश्च तथाऽसुरैः. .. 13..
3.2.m: He was astonished to behold the assembly filled with gods and excellent sages, / with gods, yakṣas, nāgas, serpents, and asuras,

3.2.s:
ṛṣibhiḥ siddhagaṃdharvaiḥ samākrāṃtocitāsanā ..
sasukhā sā sabhā brahmanna śītā na ca gharmmadā .. 14..
3.2.d:
ऋषिभिः सिद्धगंधर्वैः समाक्रांतोचितासना ..
ससुखा सा सभा ब्रह्मन्न शीता न च घर्म्मदा .. 14..
3.2.m: with seers, siddhas, and gandharvas, who had occupied appropriate seats. / That assembly was comfortable, O brahmin; it was neither cold nor hot.

3.2.s:
na kṣudhaṃ na pipāsāṃ ca na glāniṃ prāpnuvantyuta..
nānārūpairiva kṛtā maṇibhiḥ sā sabhā varaiḥ .. 19 ..
staṃbhaiśca vidhṛtā sā tu śāśvatī na ca sakṣayā ..
divyairnānāvidhairbhāvairbhāsadbhiramitaprabhā .. 16 ..
ati candraṃ ca sūryyaṃ ca śikhinaṃ ca svayaṃprabhā ..
dīpyate nākapṛṣṭhasthā bhartsayaṃtīva bhāskaram .. 17 ..
tasyām̐ sa bhagavāñchāsti vividhāndevamānuṣān ..
svayameko'niśaṃ brahmā sarvalokapitāmahaḥ .. 18 ..
upatiṣṭhaṃti cāpyenaṃ prajānāṃ patayaḥ prabhum..
dakṣaḥ pracetāḥ pulaho marīciḥ kaśyapaḥ prabhuḥ .. 19 ..
3.2.d:
न क्षुधं न पिपासां च न ग्लानिं प्राप्नुवन्त्युत..
नानारूपैरिव कृता मणिभिः सा सभा वरैः .. 19 ..
स्तंभैश्च विधृता सा तु शाश्वती न च सक्षया ..
दिव्यैर्नानाविधैर्भावैर्भासद्भिरमितप्रभा .. 16 ..
अति चन्द्रं च सूर्य्यं च शिखिनं च स्वयंप्रभा ..
दीप्यते नाकपृष्ठस्था भर्त्सयंतीव भास्करम् .. 17 ..
तस्याम्̐ स भगवाञ्छास्ति विविधान्देवमानुषान् ..
स्वयमेकोऽनिशं ब्रह्मा सर्वलोकपितामहः .. 18 ..
उपतिष्ठंति चाप्येनं प्रजानां पतयः प्रभुम्..
दक्षः प्रचेताः पुलहो मरीचिः कश्यपः प्रभुः .. 19 ..
3.2.m:
They experienced neither hunger, nor thirst, nor exhaustion. / That assembly seemed to be fashioned of diverse forms by excellent jewels,
and supported by pillars, eternal and free from decay, / of boundless splendor through radiant, diverse celestial forms.
Self-luminous, surpassing the moon, the sun, and fire, / situated on the vault of heaven, it shone as if mocking the sun.
In it, that Lord Brahmā alone, the Grandfather of all the worlds, / incessantly governs the various gods and humans.
The lords of creatures also attend upon this Lord: / Dakṣa, Pracetas, Pulaha, Marīci, and the lord Kaśyapa,

3.2.s:
bhṛguratrirvasiṣṭhaśca gautamo'tha tathāṃgirāḥ ..
pulastyaśca kratuścaiva prahlādaḥ karddamastathā .. 3.2.1.20 ..
3.2.d:
भृगुरत्रिर्वसिष्ठश्च गौतमोऽथ तथांगिराः ..
पुलस्त्यश्च क्रतुश्चैव प्रह्लादः कर्द्दमस्तथा .. 3.2.1.20 ..
3.2.m: Bhṛgu, Atri, Vasiṣṭha, Gautama, and Aṅgiras, / Pulastya, Kratu, Prahlāda, and Kardama,

3.2.s:
atharvāṃgirasaścaiva vālakhilyā marīcipāḥ ..
manoṃ'tarikṣaṃ vidyāśva vāyustejo jalaṃ mahī .. 21 ..
3.2.d:
अथर्वांगिरसश्चैव वालखिल्या मरीचिपाः ..
मनोंऽतरिक्षं विद्याश्व वायुस्तेजो जलं मही .. 21 ..
3.2.m: Atharvāṅgirases, Vālakhilyas, Marīcipas, / the mind, the sky, the Vidyās, the wind, fire, water, earth,

3.2.s:
śabdasparśau tathā rūpaṃ raso gaṃdhastathaiva ca ..
prakṛtiśca vikāraśca sadasatkāraṇaṃ tathā .. 22 ..
3.2.d:
शब्दस्पर्शौ तथा रूपं रसो गंधस्तथैव च ..
प्रकृतिश्च विकारश्च सदसत्कारणं तथा .. 22 ..
3.2.m: sound, touch, form, taste, and smell, / the primal nature, transformation, and the cause of being and non-being,

3.2.s:
agastyaśca mahātejā mārkaṃḍeyaśca vīryavān ..
jamadagnirbharadvājaḥ saṃvartaścyavanastathā .. 23 ..
3.2.d:
अगस्त्यश्च महातेजा मार्कंडेयश्च वीर्यवान् ..
जमदग्निर्भरद्वाजः संवर्तश्च्यवनस्तथा .. 23 ..
3.2.m: the greatly radiant Agastya, the valorous Mārkaṇḍeya, / Jamadagni, Bharadvāja, Saṃvarta, and Cyavana,

3.2.s:
durvāsāśca mahābhāga ṛṣyaśrṛṃgaśca dhārmikaḥ.
sanatkumāro bhagavānyogācāryyo mahātapāḥ .. 24..
3.2.d:
दुर्वासाश्च महाभाग ऋष्यश्रृंगश्च धार्मिकः.
सनत्कुमारो भगवान्योगाचार्य्यो महातपाः .. 24..
3.2.m: the illustrious Durvāsas, the righteous Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, / the venerable Sanatkumāra, master of yoga and great ascetic,

3.2.s:
asito devalaścaiva jaigīṣavyaśca tattvavit..
āyurvedastathāṣṭāṃgo gāndharvaścaiva tatra hi .. 29 ..
caṃdramāḥ sah nakṣatrairādityaśca gabhastimān ..
vāyavastaṃtavaścaiva saṃkalpaḥ prāṇa eva ca .. 26 ..
mūrtimaṃto mahātmāno mahāvrataparāyaṇāḥ ..
ete cānye ca bahavo brahmāṇaṃ samupāsire ..27..
artho dharmaśca kāmaśca harṣo dveṣastamo damaḥ ..
āyāṃti tasyāṃ sahitā gaṃdharvāpsarasāṃ gaṇāḥ .. 28..
śukrādyāśva grahāścaiva ye cānye tatsamīpagāḥ ..
maṃtrā rathaṃtaraṃ caiva harimānvasumānapi ..29..
3.2.d:
असितो देवलश्चैव जैगीषव्यश्च तत्त्ववित्..
आयुर्वेदस्तथाष्टांगो गान्धर्वश्चैव तत्र हि .. 29 ..
चंद्रमाः सह् नक्षत्रैरादित्यश्च गभस्तिमान् ..
वायवस्तंतवश्चैव संकल्पः प्राण एव च .. 26 ..
मूर्तिमंतो महात्मानो महाव्रतपरायणाः ..
एते चान्ये च बहवो ब्रह्माणं समुपासिरे ..27..
अर्थो धर्मश्च कामश्च हर्षो द्वेषस्तमो दमः ..
आयांति तस्यां सहिता गंधर्वाप्सरसां गणाः .. 28..
शुक्राद्याश्व ग्रहाश्चैव ये चान्ये तत्समीपगाः ..
मंत्रा रथंतरं चैव हरिमान्वसुमानपि ..29..
3.2.m:
Asita, Devala, and Jaigīṣavya, the knower of truth, / the eightfold Āyurveda and the Gandharva lore there,
the moon together with the constellations, the ray-filled sun, / the winds, the cosmic threads, intention, and the vital breath,
personified, great-souled, dedicated to great vows— / these and many others waited upon Brahmā.
Wealth, righteousness, desire, joy, hatred, darkness, and self-restraint; / the hosts of gandharvas and apsarases arrive there together.
The planets beginning with Śukra, and others who go near to him, / the mantras, the rathaṃtara chant, and Harimat and Vasumat,

3.2.s:
mahito viśvakarmā ca vasavaścaiva sarvaśaḥ ..
tathā pitṛgaṇāḥ sarve sarvāṇi ca havīṃṣyatha .. 3.2.1.30 ..
3.2.d:
महितो विश्वकर्मा च वसवश्चैव सर्वशः ..
तथा पितृगणाः सर्वे सर्वाणि च हवींष्यथ .. 3.2.1.30 ..
3.2.m: the revered Viśvakarman, the Vasus on all sides, / all the hosts of ancestors, and all the sacrificial oblations,

3.2.s:
ṛgvedaḥ sāmavedaśca yajurvedastathaiva ca ..
atharvavedaśca tathā sarvaśāstrāṇi caiva ha .. 31 ..
3.2.d:
ऋग्वेदः सामवेदश्च यजुर्वेदस्तथैव च ..
अथर्ववेदश्च तथा सर्वशास्त्राणि चैव ह .. 31 ..
3.2.m: the Ṛgveda, the Sāmaveda, the Yajurveda, / the Atharvaveda, and all the scriptures,

3.2.s:
itihāsopavedāśca vedāṃgāni ca sarvaśaḥ..
medhā dhṛtiḥ smṛtiścaiva prajñā buddhiryaśaḥ samāḥ.. 32 ..
3.2.d:
इतिहासोपवेदाश्च वेदांगानि च सर्वशः..
मेधा धृतिः स्मृतिश्चैव प्रज्ञा बुद्धिर्यशः समाः.. 32 ..
3.2.m: the Itihāsas, Upavedas, and all the auxiliary limbs of the Veda, / intelligence, resolve, memory, wisdom, intellect, fame, and the years,

3.2.s:
kālacakraṃ ca taddivyaṃ nityamakṣayamavyayam ..
yāvantyo devapatnyaśca sarvā eva manojavāḥ ..33..
gārhapatyā nākacarāḥ pitaro lokaviśrutāḥ ..
somapā ekaśṛṃgāśca tathā sarve tapasvinaḥ.. 31 .
3.2.d:
कालचक्रं च तद्दिव्यं नित्यमक्षयमव्ययम् ..
यावन्त्यो देवपत्न्यश्च सर्वा एव मनोजवाः ..33..
गार्हपत्या नाकचराः पितरो लोकविश्रुताः ..
सोमपा एकशृंगाश्च तथा सर्वे तपस्विनः.. 31 .
3.2.m:
the celestial wheel of time, eternal, imperishable, and unchanging, / as many wives of the gods as there are, all swift as thought,
the Gārhapatyas, dwellers in heaven, the world-renowned ancestors, / the Somapas, the Ekaśṛṅgas, and all the ascetics,

3.2.s:
nāgāḥ suparṇāḥ paśavaḥ pitāmahamupāsate .
sthāvarā jaṃgamāścāpi mahābhūtāstathā pare .. 39..
puraṃdaraśca deveṃdro varuṇo dhanadastathā..
mahādevaḥ sahomo'tra sadā gacchati sarvadaḥ .. 36..
gacchaṃti sarvadā devā nārāyaṇastatharṣayaḥ..
ṛṣayo vālakhilyāśca yonijāyonijāstathā... 37..
yatkiṃcitriṣu lokeṣu dṛśyate sthāṇu jaṃgamam ..
tasyāṃ sahopaviṣṭāyāṃ tatra jñātvā sa dharmavit .. 38 ..
devairmunivaraiḥ krāṃtāṃ samālokyātivismitaḥ..
harṣeṇa mahatā yukto romāṃcitatanūruhaḥ .. 39 ..
3.2.d:
नागाः सुपर्णाः पशवः पितामहमुपासते .
स्थावरा जंगमाश्चापि महाभूतास्तथा परे .. 39..
पुरंदरश्च देवेंद्रो वरुणो धनदस्तथा..
महादेवः सहोमोऽत्र सदा गच्छति सर्वदः .. 36..
गच्छंति सर्वदा देवा नारायणस्तथर्षयः..
ऋषयो वालखिल्याश्च योनिजायोनिजास्तथा... 37..
यत्किंचित्रिषु लोकेषु दृश्यते स्थाणु जंगमम् ..
तस्यां सहोपविष्टायां तत्र ज्ञात्वा स धर्मवित् .. 38 ..
देवैर्मुनिवरैः क्रांतां समालोक्यातिविस्मितः..
हर्षेण महता युक्तो रोमांचिततनूरुहः .. 39 ..
3.2.m:
nāgas, suparṇas, and beasts attend upon the Grandfather, / as well as the immobile and mobile beings, and other great elements.
Puraṃdara the king of gods, Varuṇa, Dhanada, / and Mahādeva with Umā, the giver of everything, always goes there.
The gods always go, and Nārāyaṇa, as well as the seers, / the seers and the Vālakhilyas, both womb-born and not womb-born.
Whatever is seen in the three worlds, stationary or moving— / knowing it to be seated together there in that assembly, that knower of dharma,
beholding it filled with gods and excellent sages, was utterly amazed; / filled with great joy, the hairs on his body stood on end.

3.2.s:
tatra dharmo mahātejāḥ kathāṃ pāpapraṇāśinīm ..
vācyamānāṃ tu śuśrāva vyāsenāmitatejasā .. 3.2.1.40 ..
3.2.d:
तत्र धर्मो महातेजाः कथां पापप्रणाशिनीम् ..
वाच्यमानां तु शुश्राव व्यासेनामिततेजसा .. 3.2.1.40 ..
3.2.m: There Dharma of great splendor heard a sin-destroying tale / being recited by Vyāsa of boundless luster:

3.2.s:
dharmāraṇyakathāṃ divyāṃ tathaiva sumanoharām ..
dharmārthakāmamokṣāṇāṃ phaladātrīṃ tathaiva ca .. 41 .
3.2.d:
धर्मारण्यकथां दिव्यां तथैव सुमनोहराम् ..
धर्मार्थकाममोक्षाणां फलदात्रीं तथैव च .. 41 .
3.2.m: the divine, utterly captivating tale of Dharmāraṇya, / which grants the fruits of dharma, wealth, pleasure, and liberation,

3.2.s:
putrapautraprapautrādi phaladātrīṃ tathaiva ca ..
dhāraṇācchravaṇāccāpi paṭhanāccāvalokanāt ..42..
3.2.d:
पुत्रपौत्रप्रपौत्रादि फलदात्रीं तथैव च ..
धारणाच्छ्रवणाच्चापि पठनाच्चावलोकनात् ..42..
3.2.m: and also bestows the fruit of sons, grandsons, and great-grandsons, / through retaining, hearing, reciting, and viewing.

3.2.s:
tāṃ niśamya suvistīrṇāṃ kathāṃ brahmāṃḍasaṃbhavām .. pra
modotphullanayano brahmāṇamanumatya ca .. 43 ..
3.2.d:
तां निशम्य सुविस्तीर्णां कथां ब्रह्मांडसंभवाम् .. प्र
मोदोत्फुल्लनयनो ब्रह्माणमनुमत्य च .. 43 ..
3.2.m: Having heard that very extensive tale born from the cosmic egg, / with eyes blossomed with joy and having obtained the leave of Brahmā,

3.2.s:
kṛtakāryopi dharmātmā gaṃtukāmastadābhavat ..
namaskṛtya tadā dharmo brahmāṇaṃ sa pitāmaham .. 44 ..
3.2.d:
कृतकार्योपि धर्मात्मा गंतुकामस्तदाभवत् ..
नमस्कृत्य तदा धर्मो ब्रह्माणं स पितामहम् .. 44 ..
3.2.m: having accomplished his purpose, the virtuous Dharma then wished to depart; / having bowed to Brahmā the Grandfather at that time,

3.2.s:
anujñātastadā tena gato'sau yamaśāsanam ..
pitāmahaprasādācca śrutvā puṇyapradāyinīm .. 45 ..
3.2.d:
अनुज्ञातस्तदा तेन गतोऽसौ यमशासनम् ..
पितामहप्रसादाच्च श्रुत्वा पुण्यप्रदायिनीम् .. 45 ..
3.2.m: Permitted by him then, he went to the domain of Yama, / and having heard, through the grace of the grandfather [Brahmā], that which bestows merit—

3.2.s:
dharmāraṇyakathāṃ divyāṃ pavitrāṃ pāpanāśinīm ..
sa gato'nucaraiḥ sārddhaṃ tataḥ saṃyaminīṃ prati .. 46..
3.2.d:
धर्मारण्यकथां दिव्यां पवित्रां पापनाशिनीम् ..
स गतोऽनुचरैः सार्द्धं ततः संयमिनीं प्रति .. 46..
3.2.m: the divine, holy story of Dharmāraṇya, which destroys sin, / he went thence together with his attendants toward Saṃyaminī.

3.2.s:
amātyānucaraiḥ sārdhaṃ praviṣṭaḥ svapuraṃ yamaḥ ..
tatrāṃtare mahātejā nārado munipuṃgavaḥ.. 47..
3.2.d:
अमात्यानुचरैः सार्धं प्रविष्टः स्वपुरं यमः ..
तत्रांतरे महातेजा नारदो मुनिपुंगवः.. 47..
3.2.m: Accompanied by ministers and attendants, Yama entered his own city. / Meanwhile, Nārada, that bull among sages of great splendor,

3.2.s:
durnirīkṣyaḥ kṛpāyuktaḥ samadarśī taponidhiḥ ..
tapasā dagdhadehopi viṣṇubhaktiparāyaṇaḥ.. 48..
3.2.d:
दुर्निरीक्ष्यः कृपायुक्तः समदर्शी तपोनिधिः ..
तपसा दग्धदेहोपि विष्णुभक्तिपरायणः.. 48..
3.2.m: hard to behold, full of compassion, impartial, a treasury of austerity, / whose body was consumed by austerity, devoted to the devotion to Viṣṇu,

3.2.s:
sarvagaḥ sarvaviccaiva nāradaḥ sarvadā śuciḥ ..
vedādhyayanaśīlaśca tvāgata statra saṃsadi ..49..
3.2.d:
सर्वगः सर्वविच्चैव नारदः सर्वदा शुचिः ..
वेदाध्ययनशीलश्च त्वागत स्तत्र संसदि ..49..
3.2.m: all-pervading, all-knowing, ever pure, / and devoted to the study of the Vedas, arrived there in that assembly.

3.2.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasā dharmo bhāryayā sevakaiḥ saha ..
saṃmukho harṣasaṃyukto gacchanneva sa satvaraḥ..3.2.1.50..
3.2.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा सहसा धर्मो भार्यया सेवकैः सह ..
संमुखो हर्षसंयुक्तो गच्छन्नेव स सत्वरः..3.2.1.50..
3.2.m: Seeing him suddenly, Dharma, together with his wife and servants, / went swiftly to meet him, filled with joy:

3.2.s:
adya me saphalaṃ janma adya me saphalaṃ kulam..
adya me saphalo dharmastvayyāyāte tapodhane ..51..
3.2.d:
अद्य मे सफलं जन्म अद्य मे सफलं कुलम्..
अद्य मे सफलो धर्मस्त्वय्यायाते तपोधने ..51..
3.2.m: "Today my birth has borne fruit! Today my lineage has borne fruit! / Today my righteousness has borne fruit, now that you have arrived, O rich in austerity!

3.2.s:
arghyapādyādividhinā pūjāṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ ..
daṃḍavattaṃ praṇamyātha vidhinā copaveśitaḥ ..52..
3.2.d:
अर्घ्यपाद्यादिविधिना पूजां कृत्वा विधानतः ..
दंडवत्तं प्रणम्याथ विधिना चोपवेशितः ..52..
3.2.m: Having duly performed worship with the rites of water for hospitality, water for feet, and the rest, / and having prostrated before him like a staff, he seated him in the proper manner

3.2.s:
āsane sve mahādivye ratnakāṃcanabhūṣite ..
citrārpitā sabhā sarvā dīpā nirvātagā iva ..53..
3.2.d:
आसने स्वे महादिव्ये रत्नकांचनभूषिते ..
चित्रार्पिता सभा सर्वा दीपा निर्वातगा इव ..53..
3.2.m: on his own great divine seat, adorned with jewels and gold. / The whole assembly [sat still] as if painted in a picture, like lamps in a windless place.

3.2.s:
vidhāya kuśalapraśnaṃ svāgatenābhinaṃdya tam ..
praharṣamatulaṃ lebhe dharmāraṇyakathāṃ smaran .. 54 ..
3.2.d:
विधाय कुशलप्रश्नं स्वागतेनाभिनंद्य तम् ..
प्रहर्षमतुलं लेभे धर्मारण्यकथां स्मरन् .. 54 ..
3.2.m: Inquiring after his welfare and welcoming him with greetings, / he attained incomparable delight as he remembered the story of Dharmāraṇya.

3.2.s:
nāradaṃ pūjayitvā tu prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā ..
harṣitaṃ tu yamaṃ dṛṣṭvā nārado vismitānanaḥ .. 55 ..
3.2.d:
नारदं पूजयित्वा तु प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना ..
हर्षितं तु यमं दृष्ट्वा नारदो विस्मिताननः .. 55 ..
3.2.m: Having worshipped Nārada with a joyful heart— / seeing Yama so delighted, Nārada was filled with wonder,

3.2.s:
ciṃtayāmāsa manasā kimidaṃ harṣito hariḥ ..
atiharṣaṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā yamarājasvarūpiṇam ..
āścaryamanasaṃ caiva nāradaḥ pṛṣṭavāṃstadā .. 56 .. ..
3.2.d:
चिंतयामास मनसा किमिदं हर्षितो हरिः ..
अतिहर्षं च तं दृष्ट्वा यमराजस्वरूपिणम् ..
आश्चर्यमनसं चैव नारदः पृष्टवांस्तदा .. 56 .. ..
3.2.m: and thought in his mind: 'What is this, that Hari [Yama] is so joyful?' / And seeing him, who has the form of Yamarāja, filled with extreme joy, / his mind full of wonder, Nārada then asked:

3.2.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
kiṃ dṛṣṭaṃ bhavatāścaryyaṃ kiṃ vā labdhaṃ mahatpadam..
duṣṭastvaṃ duṣṭakarmā ca duṣṭātmā krodharūpadhṛk .. 57..
3.2.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
किं दृष्टं भवताश्चर्य्यं किं वा लब्धं महत्पदम्..
दुष्टस्त्वं दुष्टकर्मा च दुष्टात्मा क्रोधरूपधृक् .. 57..
3.2.m: Nārada said: / 'What wondrous thing has been seen by you, or what great rank has been attained? / You are harsh, harsh in your deeds, harsh-minded, and bearing the form of wrath;

3.2.s:
pāpināṃ yamanaṃ caivametadrūpaṃ mahattaram..
saumyarūpaṃ kathaṃ jātametanme saṃśayaḥ prabho .. 58..
3.2.d:
पापिनां यमनं चैवमेतद्रूपं महत्तरम्..
सौम्यरूपं कथं जातमेतन्मे संशयः प्रभो .. 58..
3.2.m: your primary form is the restraint of sinners. / How has it become gentle? This is my doubt, O lord.

3.2.s:
adya tvaṃ harṣasaṃyukto dṛśyase kena hetunā ..
kathayasva mahākāya harṣasyaiva hi kāraṇam.. 59..
3.2.d:
अद्य त्वं हर्षसंयुक्तो दृश्यसे केन हेतुना ..
कथयस्व महाकाय हर्षस्यैव हि कारणम्.. 59..
3.2.m: Why are you seen today filled with joy? / Tell me, O large-bodied one, the cause of this joy!'

3.2.s:
.. dharmarāja uvāca .. ..
śrūyatāṃ brahmaputraitatkathayāmi na saṃśayaḥ ..
purāhaṃ brahmasadanaṃ gatavānabhivaṃditum.. 3.2.1.60 ..
3.2.d:
.. धर्मराज उवाच .. ..
श्रूयतां ब्रह्मपुत्रैतत्कथयामि न संशयः ..
पुराहं ब्रह्मसदनं गतवानभिवंदितुम्.. 3.2.1.60 ..
3.2.m: Dharmarāja said: / 'Listen, O son of Brahmā, I shall tell this without doubt. / Formerly, I went to the abode of Brahmā to pay homage.

3.2.s:
tatrāsīnaḥ sabhāmadhye sarvalokaikapūjite...
nānākathāḥ śrutāstatra dharmmavargasamanvitāḥ .. 61..
3.2.d:
तत्रासीनः सभामध्ये सर्वलोकैकपूजिते...
नानाकथाः श्रुतास्तत्र धर्म्मवर्गसमन्विताः .. 61..
3.2.m: Seated there in the midst of the assembly, worshipped by all the worlds, / various stories concerned with the matters of dharma were heard by me there,

3.2.s:
kathāḥ puṇyā dharmayutā ramyā vyāsamukhācchrutāḥ ..
dharmakāmārthasaṃyuktāḥ sarvāghaughavināśinīḥ .. 62 ..
3.2.d:
कथाः पुण्या धर्मयुता रम्या व्यासमुखाच्छ्रुताः ..
धर्मकामार्थसंयुक्ताः सर्वाघौघविनाशिनीः .. 62 ..
3.2.m: meritorious stories endowed with dharma, delightful, heard from the mouth of Vyāsa, / connected with righteousness, pleasure, and wealth, destroying all multitudes of sins,

3.2.s:
yāḥ śrutvā sarvapāpebhyo mucyaṃte brahmahatyayā .
tārayaṃti pitṛgaṇāñchatamekottaraṃ mune .. 63 .. ..
3.2.d:
याः श्रुत्वा सर्वपापेभ्यो मुच्यंते ब्रह्महत्यया .
तारयंति पितृगणाञ्छतमेकोत्तरं मुने .. 63 .. ..
3.2.m: hearing which people are freed from all sins, [even] from the murder of a brahmin, / and which deliver one hundred and one generations of ancestors, O sage.'

3.2.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
kīdṛśī tatkathā me tāṃ praśaṃsa bhavatā śrutām..
kathāṃ yama mahābāho śrotukāmosmyahaṃ ca tām .. 64 .. ..
3.2.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
कीदृशी तत्कथा मे तां प्रशंस भवता श्रुताम्..
कथां यम महाबाहो श्रोतुकामोस्म्यहं च ताम् .. 64 .. ..
3.2.m: Nārada said: / 'What is that story like? Describe to me that which was heard by you! / O mighty-armed Yama, I too desire to hear that story.'

3.2.s:
.. yama uvāca .. ..
ekadā brahmaloke'haṃ namaskartuṃ pitāmaham ..
gatavānasmi taṃ deśaṃ kāryākāryavicāraṇe .. 65..
3.2.d:
.. यम उवाच .. ..
एकदा ब्रह्मलोकेऽहं नमस्कर्तुं पितामहम् ..
गतवानस्मि तं देशं कार्याकार्यविचारणे .. 65..
3.2.m: Yama said: / 'Once, in order to pay homage to the grandfather [Brahmā], / I went to that realm, the world of Brahmā, for the discernment of what is right and wrong to do.

3.2.s:
mayā tatrādbhutaṃ dṛṣṭaṃ śrutaṃ ca munisattama ..
dharmmāraṇyakathāṃ divyāṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyaneritām.. 66..
3.2.d:
मया तत्राद्भुतं दृष्टं श्रुतं च मुनिसत्तम ..
धर्म्मारण्यकथां दिव्यां कृष्णद्वैपायनेरिताम्.. 66..
3.2.m: There a wonder was seen by me, and heard, O best of sages: / the divine story of Dharmāraṇya spoken by Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana.

3.2.s:
śrutvā kathāṃ mahāpuṇyāṃ brahmanbrahmāṃḍagāṃ śubhām ..
guṇapūrṇāṃ satyayuktāṃ tena harṣeṇa harṣitaḥ .. 67..
3.2.d:
श्रुत्वा कथां महापुण्यां ब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मांडगां शुभाम् ..
गुणपूर्णां सत्ययुक्तां तेन हर्षेण हर्षितः .. 67..
3.2.m: Having heard that very meritorious, auspicious story, O brahmin, which spans the universe, / full of virtues and endowed with truth, I am joyful with that joy.

3.2.s:
anyaccaiva muniśreṣṭha tavāgamanakāraṇam..
śubhāya ca sukhāyaiva kṣemāya ca jayāya hi .. 68..
3.2.d:
अन्यच्चैव मुनिश्रेष्ठ तवागमनकारणम्..
शुभाय च सुखायैव क्षेमाय च जयाय हि .. 68..
3.2.m: Moreover, O best of sages, the reason for your arrival / is indeed for auspiciousness, happiness, safety, and victory.

3.2.s:
ādyāsmi kṛtakṛtyo'hamadyāhaṃ sukṛtī mune.
dharmonāmādya jāto'haṃ tava padyugmadarśanāt .. 69 .
3.2.d:
आद्यास्मि कृतकृत्योऽहमद्याहं सुकृती मुने.
धर्मोनामाद्य जातोऽहं तव पद्युग्मदर्शनात् .. 69 .
3.2.m: Today I have achieved my purpose; today I am one of good deeds, O sage. / Today I have truly become Dharma by name, through the sight of your two feet.

3.2.s:
pūjyo'haṃ ca kṛtārthohaṃ dhanyohaṃ cādya nārada..
yuṣmatpādaprasādācca pūjyo'haṃ bhuvanatraye .. 3.2.1.70 ..
3.2.d:
पूज्योऽहं च कृतार्थोहं धन्योहं चाद्य नारद..
युष्मत्पादप्रसादाच्च पूज्योऽहं भुवनत्रये .. 3.2.1.70 ..
3.2.m: I am worthy of worship, my goal is achieved, and I am blessed today, O Nārada; / by the grace of your feet I am worthy of worship in the three worlds.'

Nārada said: / “This is the time for my ritual ablution; it is not the occasion for my narration. / Nevertheless, listen, O king: I will give you instruction. (104)
Māgha is the best among the months for ritual ablution, giving gifts, and the like. / And whoever bathes in that month of Māgha is freed from all sins. / Go quickly to the Gaṅgā for ritual ablution now, O king; / and Vyāsa's arrival will take place today, O best of kings. (105–106)

Whatever ancient account there is of the entire Dharmāraṇya, / Vyāsa, the son of Satyavatī, will tell you all of it.” (109)
Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, the son of Brahmā vanished right there. / When he had gone, the king amused himself with his ministers. / In the meantime, the son of Satyavatī arrived there; / then Vidura indeed announced [him] to the Pāṇḍava. (110–111)
Sūta said: / Hearing that the sage had arrived, all, filled with joy, / Bhīma and the others, along with Dharma, stood up on all sides. (112)
Then indeed, going to meet him, with head bowed he rejoiced. / Having bowed to him like a stick together with his brothers at that time, (113)
performing a very splendid worship with the honey-mixture according to rule, / and seating him upon a throne, he then inquired after his health. (114)

Yudhiṣṭhira said: / “By your grace, O brahmin, excellent tales have been heard by me, / duties in times of distress, the duties of kings, and duties for liberation in many ways, (116)
and the duties of the Purāṇas, and likewise numerous vows, / sacred fords of manifold forms, and all shrines. (117)
Now I desire to hear the auspicious tale of Dharmāraṇya, / hearing which sin such as the slaughter of a brahmin is destroyed. (118)
I wish to hear accurately of the sacred fords situated in Dharmāraṇya: / By whom was this place established? From what cause was it created? (119)

Tell me that. / How many were the brahmins, and by whom were they settled long ago? / For what purpose were the eighteen thousand settled? / From what part were those brahmins, best among the twice-born, born? / Skilled in all branches of learning, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / well-versed in the Ṛgveda and having exerted themselves in the Yajurveda, / knowing the far shore of the Sāmaveda's limbs, knowing the threefold knowledge, foremost in dharma, / devoted to austerity, of auspicious conduct, intent on vows of truth, / emaciated by month-long fasts and by cāndrāyaṇa penances and the like, / of good conduct, friendly to brahmins—by what do they make their daily livelihood? / Tell me all that entirely from the beginning, O best of speakers! / How is it that the dānavas, daiteyas, beings born as bhūtas and vetālas, / rākṣasas, and piśācas there do not torment them? / Thus ends the second chapter, titled "The Description of Yudhiṣṭhira's Questions," in the māhātmya of Dharmāraṇya, in the first half of the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the venerable Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses.

Once, Dharmarāja performed exceedingly difficult austerity

At the beginning of the Tretāyuga, O king, for thirty thousand years,
[he sat] in the middle of the forest practicing austerity at the foot of an aśoka tree,
a mass of bones held together only by dry sinews, motionless in form,
whose blood had been completely drained away by millions of anthill-dwelling insects,
a heap of fleshless bones, motionless as a crystal stone,
radiant with a luster like a conch, a jasmine blossom, the moon, snow, or a great white conch,
his vital breath sustained only by pure spirit, preserved by what remained of his lifespan,
his life indicated only by the subtle movement of inhalation and exhalation,
the small creatures [around him] made gentle by the mere movement of his opening and closing eyelids,
the quarters of the sky illuminated by his eyes that radiated flashing reddish-yellow beams,
the forest withered, kissed by the forest-fire flame of his austerity,
yet with all trees sprinkled by the shower of nectar brought forth by his peaceful calm,
as if austerity itself had assumed human form and was practicing austerity in visible presence,

there is no one superior to them in the three worlds, O descendant of Bharata. // 9

When a śrāddha is performed by men with wealth acquired unjustly,
they are satisfied through it in Caṇḍāla, Pulkasa, and other wombs.
Thus, O child, many relatives are nourished by it. If one lacks the capacity to perform a śrāddha, it can be done even with vegetables.

for one performing a śrāddha, the family never perishes anywhere.
If sin has been committed, all that sin certainly increases;

3.2.d: इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां सहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे पूर्वभागे धर्माण्यक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये धर्माचारवर्णनंनाम सप्तमोऽध्यायः .. 7 ..
3.2.m: Thus ends the seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Conduct of Dharma', in the Māhātmya of the Sacred Field of Dharmāraṇya, in the first part of the third Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skandapurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.

3.2.m: Vyāsa said: / Having reached the Dharmavāpī pool, whoever performs the water-offering to the ancestors— / the ancestors attain satisfaction for as long as the fourteen Indras rule. 1 / And the ancestors are to be worshiped here, as well as the forebears who have gone to heaven; / one should offer piṇḍas to them, having reached this [pool] which grants liberation. 2 / In the Tretā age by five days, in the Dvāpara age by three days, / but in the Kali age, O brahmins, whoever offers a piṇḍa with single-minded devotion [gains the fruit]. 3 / For in the world men have become greedy once the Kali age has arrived; / people are devoted to others' wives, and women are very fickle; 4 / all men, women, and eunuchs are intent on malice toward others, / constantly devoted to reviling others, looking for others' flaws, 5 / surely causing anxiety to others, quarrelsome, creating dissension among friends— / all of them attain purity; the masters of fate have declared this themselves. 6 / This has been spoken, O fortunate one, as the description of Dharmāraṇya / and all the fruit here which was declared by the trident-bearing [Śiva]: 7 / pure in speech, mind, and body, averting their faces from others' wives, / free from malice, even-minded when angered, devoted to mother and father, 8 / free from fickleness, devoid of greed, devoted to the duty of giving, / believing, knowing righteousness, and dedicated to devotion to their master; 9 / and a devoted wife who is dedicated to serving her husband; / harmless, hospitable, and always delighting in their own duty. 3.2.7.10 / Śaunaka said: / Listen, O fortunate Sūta, best of all knowers of righteousness: / The good conduct of householders has been heard by me from your mouth. 11 / Tell me today one thing desired by my mind, O Sūta's son: / Tell me, of what nature are the characteristics of all devoted wives? 12 / Sūta said: / He in whose home there is a devoted wife, his life is fruitful; / she who is like a shadow of his body, whose conduct generates merit. 13 / Devoted wives are equal to Arundhatī, Sāvitrī, and Anasūyā, / to Śāṇḍilyā, Satyā, Lakṣmī, Śatarūpā, 14 / Menā, Sunīti, Saṃjñā, and Svāhā.

3.2.m:
The duties of faithful wives were indeed proclaimed by the sage:
She eats after her husband has eaten, and she stands waiting upon him.
She sleeps after he has fallen asleep, and awakens before [him].
She keeps herself unadorned when her husband is in a foreign land;
when he has gone abroad on business anywhere, she is completely stripped of ornaments.
She does not utter her husband's name, indeed for the increase of his life;
nor does she ever utter the name of another man.
Even when reviled she should not revile him, and even when struck she is gracious;
she says: "Let it be considered, master, that this which was to be done is done."
When summoned, she abandons household chores and goes swiftly:
"For what purpose was I called, lord? Let that favor be bestowed."
She does not stand long at the doorway, nor does she frequent the doorway.
She never gives away on her own anything that should not be given.
Without being told, she prepares on her own all the articles of worship,
where the water for vows, the darbha grass, flowers, unbroken grains, and the like [are kept].
Anticipating [his wishes], whatever is appropriate for the time,
she should set it all before him, cheerful and without irritation.
She consumes the leftovers of her husband's desirable food, fruits, and the like.
She should avoid from afar watching public gatherings and festivals;
she should not go on pilgrimages to sacred fords, to watch weddings, and such things.
When he is happily asleep, sitting at ease, or amusing himself at will,
she should never wake her husband, even if there is an obstacle in affairs.
During her menstrual period, for three nights she must not show her face,
nor make her speech heard, until she is purified by bathing.
Having bathed well, she should look at the face of her husband and never that of another;
or, meditating upon her husband in her mind, she may look at the sun.
Turmeric, saffron, vermilion, and collyrium,
a bodice, betel, auspicious ornaments,
the dressing of hair, and ornaments for the hands, ears, and so forth—

3.2.m:
wishing for her husband's long life, the faithful wife should not put [these] away.
She never converses with a woman who hates her husband.
She should never be alone anywhere, nor should she ever bathe naked.
Neither on a mortar, nor on a pestle, nor on a broom, nor on a grinding-stone,
nor on an oil-press, nor on the threshold should a virtuous woman ever sit.
Except at the time of sexual union, she should nowhere display boldness.
Wherever her husband has a liking, there she is always full of love.
This alone is the vow of women, this alone is the supreme virtue,
and this alone is worship: she must not transgress the word of her husband.
Whether he is impotent, in distress, diseased, or old,
well-situated or destitute, she must not transgress her husband alone.
Even when ghee, salt, asafoetida, and the like are exhausted, a faithful wife
should not say to her husband, "There is none," nor serve him in iron vessels.
Desiring the bath of a sacred ford, she should drink the water from her husband's feet.
For a woman, her husband is even greater than Śaṃkara or Viṣṇu.
She who observes vows, fasts, and observances by transgressing her husband
takes away her husband's longevity, and having died, she goes to hell.
When addressed, the woman who gives a retorting answer, full of anger,
becomes a female dog in a village, or a female jackal in a deserted forest.
For women, one supreme observance has been declared:
having worshipped the feet of her husband, she should eat with a resolute mind.
She should not occupy an elevated seat, nor go to the houses of others;
there she should never utter harsh words,
nor should she speak loudly or shout in the presence of elders.
The evil-minded woman who, abandoning her husband, wanders in secret,
becomes a cruel female owl dwelling in the hollow of a tree.
If, being struck, she strikes him, she becomes a tigress or a female cat;
she who casts sidelong glances at another man becomes cross-eyed.
She who, abandoning her husband, eats sweet foods alone—

3.2.m:
she becomes a female sow in a village, or a dung-eating bat.
She who speaks unpleasantly, crying out in defiance, truly becomes mute.
She who constantly envies her co-wife becomes wretched birth after birth.
She who, averting her eyes from her husband, looks at another,
becomes one-eyed, or deformed-faced, or ugly.
Seeing him arriving from outside, she hurries with water and a seat,
with betel leaves, fans, and foot massage and the like,
and likewise with charming words and excellent wiping of sweat;
she who, being pleased, satisfies her beloved—by her the three worlds are satisfied.
A father gives in limited measure, a brother gives in limited measure, a son gives a son;
who would not worship a husband, the giver of limitless [blessings]?
The husband is a deity, the husband is a guru, the husband is dharma, sacred fords, and vows;
therefore, casting aside everything, one should worship the husband alone.
Just as an embodied being devoid of life attains impurity in an instant,
so a woman devoid of her husband, though well-bathed, is always impure.
A widow is more inauspicious than all inauspicious things;
from the sight of a widow, success never arises anywhere.
Excepting one's mother alone, all [widows] are devoid of auspiciousness;
a wise man should shun even their blessing as if it were a venomous snake.
At the time of a maiden's wedding, the twice-born should pronounce:
"May she be her husband's companion whether he is living or deceased."
Joyfully following her husband from the house to the cremation ground,
she undoubtedly attains the fruit of an Aśvamedha sacrifice at every step.
Just as a snake-catcher forcibly draws a serpent from its hole,
so the virtuous wife, having snatched her husband from the messengers, ascends to heaven.
The messengers of Yama flee upon seeing that faithful wife;
surely the sun is burned, and fire itself is consumed,
and all lusters tremble upon seeing the majesty of fidelity to a husband.
For as many tens of millions of years as the number of hairs on her body,
the faithful wife, rejoicing with her husband, enjoys the bliss of heaven.

3.2.m: Blessed is that mother in the world, and blessed indeed is that father, / and blessed is that fortunate husband in whose house there is a devoted wife. / Three ancestral lines on the father's side, three on the mother's side, and three on the husband's side / enjoy heavenly delights through the merit of a devoted wife. / But wicked women, through breach of virtue, bring down the three families; / causing sorrow here and in the next world to father, mother, and husband. / Wherever the foot of a devoted wife touches the ground, / that place of a sacred ford is to be revered; there is no greater purifier than this. / Even the Sun, out of awe, touches the devoted wife; / Soma and the Gandharva do so too, only for their own purification, not otherwise. / The waters constantly long for the touch of a devoted wife. / Destruction of sins does not come merely by the Gāyatrī; she destroys sins through her devotion to her husband. / Are there not in every house women proud of their beauty and charm? / But a devoted wife is obtained only through devotion to the Lord of the Universe. / The wife is the root of the householder, the wife is the root of happiness; / the wife is indeed for the fruit of dharma, the wife is for the increase of offspring. / Both worlds, the other world and this world, are conquered through a wife; / and the satisfaction of gods, ancestors, and guests in the house comes through a wife. / He alone should be known as a householder in whose house is a devoted wife. / Just as the body becomes purified by plunging into the Gaṅgā, / so a house becomes purified by seeing a devoted wife. / A widow sleeping on a bed causes her husband to fall; / therefore sleeping on the ground should be practiced, desiring the husband's happiness. / Anointing the limbs with ointments should never be done by a widow; / she should never enjoy fragrant substances. / A daily tarpaṇa should be made for her husband with water, kuśa grass, and sesame seeds, / as well as for his father and his grandfather, reciting their names, gotras, and so forth. / Worship of Viṣṇu should be performed with the thought that he is her husband, and not otherwise.

skilled in all virtues of righteousness, versed in every scripture,
renowned in austerity and knowledge, devoted to the recitation of the Veda—
all these seers, eighteen thousand in number, were settled [there].
Brought from various regions, they were settled there by the gods,
along with many hermitages fashioned there by the lords of creation.
In accordance with the instruction on righteousness, by Kṛṣṇa, Brahmā, and Śiva,
Keśava established them in their respective places as appropriate.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
From which lineage were born these brahmins who have crossed to the end of the Vedas,
who were established along with their households, surrounded by sons and grandsons,
accompanied by many disciples, and devoted to the agnihotra?

3.2.s: teṣāṃ sthānāni nāmāni yathāvacca vadasva me .. 23 .. ..
3.2.d: तेषां स्थानानि नामानि यथावच्च वदस्व मे .. 23 .. ..
3.2.m: Tell me properly their settlements and their names.
Vyāsa said:
Listen, O tiger among kings, regarding the dwellers of Dharmāraṇya,
the great-souled brahmins, the seers of upward-drawn seed;

3.2.s: teṣāṃ vai putrapautrāṇāṃ nāmāni ca vadāmyaham .. 25 ..
3.2.d: तेषां वै पुत्रपौत्राणां नामानि च वदाम्यहम् .. 25 ..
3.2.m: I shall tell you their names and those of their sons and grandsons.
There are twenty-four clans of the twice-born, O bull of the Pāṇḍavas.
Their branches and sub-branches, as well as sons, grandsons, and the like—
many sons were born, by hundreds and thousands.
I shall declare to you the names of the twenty-four primary [clans].
The seers of the twice-born are declared; hear also their ancestral lineages:

3.2.s: bhāradvājastathā vatsaḥ kauśikaḥ kuśa eva ca ..
3.2.d: भारद्वाजस्तथा वत्सः कौशिकः कुश एव च ..
3.2.m: Bhāradvāja, Vatsa, Kauśika, and Kuśa,
Śāṇḍilya, Kāśyapa, Gautama, and Chāndhana,
Jātūkarṇya, Vatsa, Vasiṣṭha, and Dhāraṇa,
Ātreya, Bhāṇḍila, and Laukika; after these,
Kṛṣṇāyana, Upamanyu, Gārgya, Mudgala, Mauṣaka,
Puṇyāsana, Parāśara, and after that Kauṇḍinya,
and also Gānyāsana—these are the twenty-four ancestral lineages.

3.2.s: jāmadagnyasya gotrasya pravarāḥ paṃca eva hi .. 31 ..
3.2.d: जामदग्न्यस्य गोत्रस्य प्रवराः पंच एव हि .. 31 ..
3.2.m: For the clan of Jāmadagnya, there are five ancestral sages:
Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnuvāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnika.
These five are celebrated, famous throughout the world, O king.
Born from such clans, the brahmins, masters of the Vedas,
engaged in worship of the twice-born and devoted to performing various sacrifices,
were endowed with virtue and committed to the six duties.
Such illustrious twice-born had come from diverse lands.

3.2.s: bhāmevasaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ca pravarāḥ paṃca eva hi ..
3.2.d: भामेवसं तृतीयं च प्रवराः पंच एव हि ..
3.2.m: […] the third, and there are five ancestral sages:
joined as Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnuvāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya.
Ātreya, Arcanānasa, and Śyāvāśva is the third.
The brahmins born in this clan are harsh and cunning,
wealthy, steadfast in duty, and versed in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
all devoted to gift-giving and enjoyment, acknowledged in Vedic and traditional rites.
Those of the Māṇḍavya clan should be known as endowed with five ancestral sages:
Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Atri, Āpnuvāna, and Aurva.
Brahmins born in this clan are devoted to Vedic revelation and tradition,

3.2.s: rogiṇo lobhino duṣṭā yajane yājane ratāḥ ..

3.2.m: afflicted with disease, greedy, harsh, yet engaged in sacrificing and conducting sacrifices,
all devoted to sacred rites, the Māṇḍavyas, O best of Kurus.

3.2.s: gārgyasya gotre ye jātāsteṣāṃ tu pravarāstrayaḥ ..

3.2.m: Those born in the clan of Gārgya have three ancestral sages:
Aṅgiras, Ambarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva is the third.
Those born in this clan are of upright conduct, truthful in speech,
tranquil, varied in complexion, poor, and wearing ragged garments,
endowed with affection for their company, and steadfast in the Vedic scriptures.

3.2.s: vatsagotre dvijā bhūpa pravarāḥ paṃca eva hi .. 42 ..
3.2.d: वत्सगोत्रे द्विजा भूप प्रवराः पंच एव हि .. 42 ..
3.2.m: For the twice-born of the Vatsa clan, O king, there are indeed five ancestral sages:
Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnuvāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnika.
By these [seers], indeed, five are renowned. The twice-born embody the nature of Brahman;
they are tranquil, self-restrained, virtuous, and well-endowed with righteous sons.
Though destitute of Vedic recitation, they are skilled in all rites,
handsome, well-behaved, and steadfast in all duties.

3.2.s: dānadharma ratāḥ sarve annadā jaladā dvijāḥ .. 45 ..
3.2.d: दानधर्म रताः सर्वे अन्नदा जलदा द्विजाः .. 45 ..
3.2.m: All are devoted to the virtue of giving; the twice-born are givers of food and givers of water,
compassionate, virtuous, and devoted to the welfare of all beings.
The Kāśyapa brahmins, O king, are endowed with three ancestral sages:
Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, and Naidhruva is the third.
They are knowers of the Veda, fair-complexioned, committed to vows, and performers of sacrifices,
fond of fine garments, highly capable, and always devoted to revering their gurus.
Possessed of honor and reputation, and devoted to the welfare of all beings,
these twice-born scions of Kāśyapa perform great sacrifices.
Those born in the Dhārīṇa lineage are endowed with three ancestral sages:
namely, Agasti, Darvi, Śvetāśva, [or] Dadhyavāhana.
Those who are born in this lineage, though dedicated to religious rites,
are all cruel in their deeds, and likewise pot-bellied.
With pendulous ears and large tusks, these twice-born are devoted to wealth,
wrathful, spiteful, and terrifying to all living beings.
Those brahmins who originate from Laugākṣa are dedicated to truth.
Their three ancestral sages embody knowledge of reality:
Kaśyapa, Vatsa, and Vasiṣṭha as the third.
Renowned for good conduct, they are Vaiṣṇavas of varied occupations,
covered with abundant body hair, dark-complexioned brahmins,
tranquil, generous, of good character, and always faithful to their own wives.
Those born in the Kuśika lineage are endowed with three ancestral sages:
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Audala—these three.

3.2.s: asmingotre tu ye jātā durbalā dīnamānasāḥ .. 56 ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्गोत्रे तु ये जाता दुर्बला दीनमानसाः .. 56 ..
3.2.m: Those born in this lineage are weak and depressed in mind,
untruthful-speaking brahmins, handsome, O best of kings,
skilled in all sciences, brahmins foremost among knowers of Brahman.
Those belonging to the Upamanyu lineage are endowed with three ancestral sages:
Vasiṣṭha, Bharadvāja, and Indrapramada.

3.2.s: asmingotre tu ye viprāḥ krūrāḥ kuṭilagāminaḥ ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्गोत्रे तु ये विप्राः क्रूराः कुटिलगामिनः ..
3.2.m: The brahmins born in this lineage are cruel, devious in conduct,
fault-finding, malicious, vile, intent on hoarding everything,
skilled at stirring up quarrels, wealthy, and arrogant,
ever wicked and devoted to keeping bad company,
diseased, weak, and devoid of legitimate livelihoods.
The brahmins born in the Vātsya lineage are endowed with five ancestral sages:
Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnuvāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya.
The brahmins born in this lineage are stout and possessed of vast intellect,
engaged in all rites, and steadfast in all duties,
skilled in the meaning of the Vedas and treatises, devoted to sacrificing and officiating for others,
virtuous in conduct, handsome, and far-sighted in intellect.
Those belonging to the Vātsyāyana lineage are endowed with five ancestral sages:
Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnuvāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya.
These previously mentioned ancestral sages have been declared to you, O Bhārata.

3.2.s: asmingotre tu ye jātā pākayajñaratāḥ sadā ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्गोत्रे तु ये जाता पाकयज्ञरताः सदा ..
3.2.m: Those born in this lineage are ever devoted to domestic sacrifices;
greedy and wrathful, they produce numerous progeny.
Ever devoted to ablutions, gifts, and the like, with senses restrained,
constructors of stepwells, wells, and ponds by the thousands,
constant in vows and discerning of virtues, yet foolish and bereft of the Vedas.
Those born in the Kauśika lineage are endowed with three ancestral sages:
Viśvāmitra, Aghamarṣaṇa, and Kauśika as the third.

3.2.s: asmingotre ca ye jātā brāhmaṇā brahmavedinaḥ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्गोत्रे च ये जाता ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मवेदिनः..
3.2.m: The brahmins born in this lineage are knowers of Brahman,
tranquil, restrained, virtuous, and dedicated to all duties,
yet childless, rough, and devoid of brilliance, though best of the twice-born.
Those belonging to the Bhāradvāja lineage are endowed with five ancestral sages:
Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, Bhāradvāja, Sainyasa,

3.2.s: gārgyaścai veti vijñeyāḥ pravarāḥ paṃca eva ca .. 71 ..
3.2.d: गार्ग्यश्चै वेति विज्ञेयाः प्रवराः पंच एव च .. 71 ..
3.2.m: and Gārgya—these are to be known as the five ancestral sages.

3.2.s: asmingotre ca ye jātā vāḍavā dhaninaḥ śubhāḥ ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्गोत्रे च ये जाता वाडवा धनिनः शुभाः ..
3.2.m: The brahmins born in this lineage are wealthy, auspicious,
adorned with clothes and ornaments, and devoted to reverence for the twice-born.
Devoted entirely to feeding brahmins, intent upon all righteous duties.
Those who were born in the lineage of Kaśyapa have three ancestral seers:
Kaśyapa, Apavatsāra, and Raibhya—these three are celebrated.
The brahmins born in this gotra have red eyes and fierce glances;
They are all addicted to the pleasures of the tongue, yet all of them seek the highest truth;
They are poor and diseased, thieves and speakers of falsehood;
They are ignorant of the meaning of the śāstras and devoid of the Veda and smṛti.

3.2.s: śunakeṣu ca ye jātā viprā dhyānaparāyaṇāḥ .. 76 ..
3.2.d: शुनकेषु च ये जाता विप्रा ध्यानपरायणाः .. 76 ..
3.2.m: And the brahmins born among the Śunakas are intent on meditation,
Practitioners of austerity, yogins, masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
Virtuous, of good conduct, and devoted to the worship of Viṣṇu,
Short in stature, of varied complexion, having many women, best of the twice-born,
Compassionate, straightforward, peaceful, and intent on feeding brahmins.
Those born among the Śaunakas possess three ancestral seers:
Bhārgava, Śaunahotra, and Gārtsapramada—these are the three.
The brahmins born in this region are irresistible, O king,
Very fierce, large-bodied, tall, and arrogant with pride,
Distressing in form, dark-complexioned, and learned in all the śāstras,
Voracious eaters, proud, capable, free from passion and hatred,
Adorned with fine garments and ornaments, indeed, brahmins who expound the Veda.
Those who are born in the gotra of Vasiṣṭha possess three ancestral seers:
Vasiṣṭha, Bhāradvāja, and Indrapramada.
The brahmins born in this gotra are masters of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
Sacrificers, inclined to sacrifice, sweet-voiced, and happy,
Spiteful, wealthy, possessing sons, and virtuous,
Broad-chested, O king, heroic, and destroyers of foes.

3.2.s: gautamasagotre ye jātāḥ pravarāḥ paṃca eva hi .. 85 ..
3.2.d: गौतमसगोत्रे ये जाताः प्रवराः पंच एव हि .. 85 ..
3.2.m: Those born in the gotra of Gautama indeed have five ancestral seers:
Kautsa, Gārgya, Somavāha, Asita, and Devala.

3.2.s: asmingotre ca ye jātā viprāḥ paramapāvanāḥ .. 86 ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्गोत्रे च ये जाता विप्राः परमपावनाः .. 86 ..
3.2.m: The brahmins born in this gotra are exceedingly purifying,
All benefactors of others, devoted to the śruti and smṛti;
They sit like herons, are deceitful, and are intent on fraudulent conduct;
Skilled in the meaning of various śāstras, adorned with various ornaments,
Skilled in work with trees and [gardening], slow to forgive anger, and sickly.
Those born in the gotra of Aṅgiras possess three ancestral seers:
Āṅgirasa, Ambarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva as the third.

3.2.s: asmingotre ca ye jātāḥ satya saṃbhāṣiṇastathā ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्गोत्रे च ये जाताः सत्य संभाषिणस्तथा ..
3.2.m: Those born in this gotra speak the truth,
Have conquered their senses, are handsome, eat little, and have auspicious faces,
Observant of great vows, knowers of the Purāṇas, devoted to making great gifts,
Free from malice, yet prone to greed, intent upon Vedic study,
Farsighted, of great splendor, yet deluded by great māyā.
Those in the gotra of Śāṇḍilya possess three ancestral seers:
Asita, Devala, and Śāṇḍilya as the third.
The fortunate, best of the twice-born born in this gotra are hunchbacked,
Afflicted with eye-diseases, very wicked, capable of great renunciation, short-lived,
Skilled in inciting quarrels, intent upon amassing everything,
Dirty, proud, and learned in the science of astrology.
Those born in the gotra of Atri possess five ancestral seers:
Ātreya, Arcanānasa, Śyāvāśva, Aṅgiras, and Atri.

3.2.s: asminvaṃśe ca ye jātā dvijāste sūryavarcasaḥ .. 96 ..
3.2.d: अस्मिन्वंशे च ये जाता द्विजास्ते सूर्यवर्चसः .. 96 ..
3.2.m: The twice-born born in this lineage possess the splendor of the sun;
Cool as the moon, all settled in Dharmāraṇya,
Of good conduct, highly capable, devoted to the śruti and śāstras,
Sacrificers, of auspicious conduct, devoted to truth and purity,
Knowers of dharma, generous, stainless, and highly enthusiastic,
Devoted to austerity and recitation of the Veda, dedicated to justice and dharma.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
Tell me, O mighty-armed one, the nectar-like tale of Dharmāraṇya,
Hearing which one is liberated from terrible sin, even from the killing of a brahmin.
Vyāsa said:
Listen, O king! I shall tell this story which is very difficult to obtain.
Yakṣas, rākṣasas, piśācas, and others began to harass the brahmins.
There was a yakṣa named Jṛmbhaka near Dharmāraṇya.
He constantly harassed the dwellers of Dharmāraṇya.
Then those foremost of twice-born [brahmins] reported to the gods:
“O gods, we are utterly oppressed by the yakṣas, rakṣasas, and other [beings].
Out of fear of them we shall today abandon this excellent place; of this there is no doubt.”
Then, by the gods together with the gandharvas, there were established upon the earth
the siddhas, excellent yoginīs, Śrīmātṛ and the others,
for the protection of the brahmins, desiring the welfare of the worlds.
Then a yoginī was established for each respective gotra.

3.2.s: yasya gotrasya yā śaktī rakṣaṇe pālane kṣamā ..

3.2.m: Śrīmātā, the goddess Tāraṇī, Āśāpūrī the guardian of gotras,
Icchārtināśinī, Pippalī, Vikāravaśā,
Jaganmātā, Mahāmātā, Siddhā, Bhaṭṭārikā, and likewise

3.2.s: kadaṃbā vikarā mīṭhā suparṇā vasujā tathā ..9..
3.2.d: कदंबा विकरा मीठा सुपर्णा वसुजा तथा ..9..
3.2.m: Kadambā, Vikarā, Mīṭhā, Suparṇā, and Vasujā,

3.2.d: मातंगी च महादेवी वाणी च मुकुटेश्वरी ..
3.2.m: Mātaṅgī, Mahādevī, Vāṇī, Mukuṭeśvarī,

3.2.s: bhadrī caiva mahāśaktiḥ saṃhārī ca mahābalā..3.2.9.110..
3.2.d: भद्री चैव महाशक्तिः संहारी च महाबला..3.2.9.110..
3.2.m: Bhadrī the great śakti, Saṃhārī endowed with great power,
and Cāmuṇḍā the great goddess—these are the gotra mothers.
They were established for protection there by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the others.
The foremost brahmins, ever devoted to their own duty, worship them.

3.2.s: tataḥ prabhṛti yoginyaḥ svesve kāle surakṣitāḥ ..12..
3.2.d: ततः प्रभृति योगिन्यः स्वेस्वे काले सुरक्षिताः ..12..
3.2.m: From then on, well protected by the yoginīs at their respective times,
the brahmins attained peace of mind, surrounded by sons and grandsons.
Then the gods together with the gandharvas, their minds filled with joy,
mounted excellent aerial chariots and departed to heaven, those nectar-eaters.
When a hundred years had elapsed, O king, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara,
remembering Dharmāraṇya out of curiosity to see it,
came there at dawn when the sun had risen, O king,
having mounted an excellent aerial chariot, attended by hosts of apsarases,
being praised in song by gandharvas and lauded by heralds.
There in that place, O king, the twice-born, [seeking] abundant kindling, flowers, and kuśa grass,
had left those hermitages and gone off in all ten directions.
Beholding that hermitage-site deserted, Maheśvara,
knower of dharma, spoke words: “O Lord, it troubles the brahmins.
Indeed, one should create an attendant for the sake of service; such is my thought.”
Having heard the words of Śambhu, Janārdana, the god of gods,
saying “True, true!”, addressed Brahmā thus:
“O Brahmā, create [attendants] for the service of the twice-born,
so that creation may be enduring today and the community of twice-born may be happy.”
Having heard the words of Viṣṇu, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds,
recollected the wish-granting cow Kāmadhenu; and immediately upon that recollection,
that cow arrived there in sacred Dharmāraṇya.

3.2.m:
And the great warrior kṣatriyas were assigned to servitude. / Then all the gods departed as they were, O king. / When the gods had gone, all those twice-born dwelt in that place. / Together with their sons and grandsons, O king, they lived free from all fear. / Knowing the Vedas, they recited the Vedas, here and there expounding the meaning of the scriptures. / Some chanted Viṣṇu here, while others chanted Śiva; / some chanted Brahmā, and some the Yama hymn. / The sacrificers performed sacrifices and tended the sacred fire, / and with the sounds of svāhā, svadhā, and vaṣaṭ, O man of virtuous vows, / the entire three worlds, moving and unmoving, were filled. / And the merchants, highly skilled and eager to serve the twice-born, / dwelt fully devoted in the auspicious, divine Dharmāraṇya. / Food, drink, and everything else—firewood, kuśa grass, fruits, and the like— / those merchants, born of cows, supplied to the twice-born. / Bringing heaps of flowers and offerings, washing bathing-cloths and garments, / plastering with cow dung and the like, sweeping, and other auspicious tasks, / threshing, grinding, and such duties were performed by the merchants' wives; / and by the command of the lord of Kāñcī, they attended upon those brahmins. / At that time all the twice-born were at ease, filled with joy; / day and night, at both twilights, they worshipped the lord of Kāñcī and the others.
Thus ends the tenth chapter, titled “The Description of the Merchants' Acceptance,” in the Dharmāraṇyamāhātmya of the first part of the Brahmakhaṇḍa in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a collection of eighty-one thousand verses.

3.2.m: Vyāsa said: / Listen, O king, to what happened in Dharmāraṇya, considered auspicious, / which I shall relate, destroying heaps of all sins. / Urged then by the Lord of the unborm [Viṣṇu], the self-manifest [Brahmā], O king, / summoned Kāmadhenu and spoke to her: / “Provide attendants for the brahmins, for each twice-born man / provide two pure-souled ones; O mother, be gracious to me!” / Saying “So be it,” the great cow marked the ground with milk; / from her bellow there came forth men wearing tufts of hair and sacred threads: / thirty-six thousand merchants endowed with great strength, / wearing the sacred thread, highly skilled, versed in all treatises, / endowed with devotion to the twice-born, pious, possessing austerity, / knowing the Purāṇas, of good conduct, righteous, feeding brahmins. / In heaven the gods praise the dwellers of Dharmāraṇya, / transcending the senses at all times in austerity, study, and gifting. / To each twice-born was given a pair of attendants; / and whatever was the gotra of the brahmin previously declared, O king, / that same gotra belonged mutually to him and to his attendant. / Having thus made this arrangement, they dwelt there on the land. / And then discipleship and attendants were granted on earth by the gods; / all was explained by Brahmā for their mutual benefit: / “Carry out their command and give whatever is desired; / bring kindling, flowers, kuśa grass, and the rest day by day. / Conduct yourselves by their permission; never show disrespect. / The natal rite, naming, and auspicious first feeding of solids, / tonsure, investiture with the sacred thread, the Mahānāmnī vows and the like, / whatever ritual action and work, observance, donation, or fast, / must be performed with their permission.” The lords of creation said this: / “If someone begins a rite without their permission, / whether the new-moon day ritual, ancestral rites, or anything auspicious or inauspicious,”

Saying "So be it," the gods, the best of immortals headed by Indra,
all offered praise, standing before Kāmadhenu.
Having achieved their aim, the gods Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Maheśvara [said]:
"You are the mother of all the gods, and you are the cause of the sacrifice.
You are the sacred ford of all sacred fords; reverence always to you, O sinless one,
on whose forehead are the Moon, Sun, and Dawn, and the Bull-bannered [Śiva];
and Sarasvatī in your roar, and all the serpents in your dewlap;
and on the hoof-backs the gandharvas and the four Vedas;
at the front of your face are all sacred fords, immobile and moving!"
And when she had been pleased with such words in manifold ways,
the cow, well pleased, said, "What shall I do?"
The gods said:
"All these auspicious attendants have been created by you, O mother goddess!
By your grace, O fortunate one, the brahmins have become happy."
Then that renowned Surabhi went to heaven, O king,
and Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, and the others disappeared right there.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
"Those attendants, born of the cow, possessing great splendor, were wifeless.
How were they wed, O holy one? When were their sons born?"
Vyāsa said:
"For their marriage, wives were brought there and arranged
from the daughters of the gandharvas by Rudra and Yama."
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
"Who was that king of the gandharvas, what was his name, and where did he dwell?
How many were his daughters, and what was their conduct? Tell me!"
Vyāsa said:
"The king of the gandharvas is known as Viśvāvasu, O king.
Sixty thousand daughters dwell in his abode.
His home, the auspicious gandharva city, is in the mid-region.

Those auspicious daughters born of the gandharva are youthful and beautiful.
Rudra’s two attendants, Nandin and Bhṛṅgin of auspicious faces, O king,
having seen those maidens previously, reported to Śiva:
"Formerly, O Mahādeva, in the gandharva city, O all-pervading lord,
countless thousands of maidens were seen in the house of Viśvāvasu.
Bring them by force, O lord, and grant them to the cow-born ones!"
Having heard this, the god Sadāśiva, slayer of Tripura,
sent a messenger named Vijaya, O descendant of Bharata.
He went there where Viśvāvasu the subduer of enemies resided,
and spoke words that were wholesome and uttered by Śiva:
"In Dharmāraṇya, O fortunate one, [brahmins] were created by the unborn lord;
brahmins who have mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary branches were settled there.
For their service, Kāmadhenu was requested.
By her, merchants of good conduct, not born from a womb, were produced:
thirty-six thousand youths, possessed of great strength.
Sent by Śiva, I have indeed come into your presence
for the sake of the maidens, O fortunate one! Give them, give them!" he said.
The gandharva said:
"Passing over all the gods and the gandharvas, O noble-minded one,
how shall I give [them] to men in the world?"
Having heard his words, Vijaya then returned,
and reported all that great conduct of the gandharva.
Vyāsa said:
Then, overcome with anger, the blessed one, who brings peace to the world,

and then the gods, as well as nāgas, bhūtas, vetālas, and sky-farers,
overcome with great wrath, arrived by the thousands.
A great tumult arose as that army advanced.
The goddess Earth trembled, and the guardians of the quarters were agitated by fear;

Vyāsa said:
Seeing that great army arrive, trembling with fear,
they all fled from the gandharva city in the ten directions.
Abandoning the city, the king of the gandharvas went to Meru, O king.
Taking all those maidens endowed with youth, beauty, and nobility,
he then gave them to the merchants, O king,
according to the rite prescribed in the Vedas, and in the presence of the gods.
Having then given the portion of clarified butter to the gandharva, the cow-born ones
then gave the portion of clarified butter to the gods, the ancestors, the Sun, the Moon,
Yama, and Mṛtyu.
Having duly offered the portions of clarified butter, those of auspicious vows took [them as wives].
From then on, when a gandharva marriage takes place,
they thoroughly receive a portion of clarified butter from all sides even today.
Those thirty-six thousand youths whom they offered,
their sons and grandsons [numbered] in the hundreds and thousands.
Therefore all of them were indeed created for servitude.
Yudhiṣṭhira said:
Tell me, O best of the twice-born: what happened after this?
Having drunk the nectar of your speech, my lord, I am not satiated.
Vyāsa said:

Having conquered all the worlds, he arrived at Dharmāraṇya.

resorting to the five fires, looking down and inhaling smoke.

The fruit that belongs to a thousand horse-sacrifices performed with abundant priestly fees—
that fruit does a person obtain, both hearer and reciting speaker.
The childless obtains sons; the poor will obtain wealth;
one obtains long life, health, and sovereign power, there is no doubt in this.
Whatever threefold evil is born of mind, speech, and body,
all that goes to destruction from remembering and proclaiming it, O king.
It is auspicious, fame-conferring, life-giving, and brings happiness and offspring;
should one listen to the māhātmya, dear one, he will be endowed with all happiness.
Whatever merit is in all sacred fords, whatever fruit in all gifts,
and whatever merit is gained by all sacrifices, is produced by hearing [this], O king.

3.2.m: Of the Aupamanyava gotra and pravara, the gotra-deity is Gātrā; [their pravaras are] Vasiṣṭha, Bharadvāja, and Indrapramada. Of the Vyāsa gotra, the gotra-deity is Jñānajā, with three pravaras: Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, and Raibhya. Of the Māṇḍavya sagotra, the gotrajā is Dārabhaṭṭārikā, with five pravaras: Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni. Of the Kuśika sagotra, the gotrajā is Tāraṇī of great strength, with three pravaras: Viśvāmitra, Devarāja, and Uddālaka. Of the Śaunaka sagotra, the gotra-deity is Śāntā, with three pravaras: Bhārgava, Vaitahavya, and Gārtsamada. Of the Kṛṣṇātreya sagotra, the gotra-deity is Bhadrayoginī, with three pravaras: Ātreya, Arcanānasa, and Śyāvāśva. Of the Gārgyāyaṇa sagotra, the gotrajā is Śāntā, with five pravaras: Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni. Of the Gārgāyaṇa gotra, the gotrajā is Jñānajā, with five pravaras: Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, Śāṇḍilya, Asita, and Devala. Of the Gāṅgeya sagotra, the deity is Śāntā Dvāravāsinī, with three pravaras: Gārgya, Gārgi, and Śaṅkhalikhita. Of the Paiṅgya sagotra, the gotrajā is Jñānajā Śeṣalaudhā, with the pravara: Āṅgirasa, Āmbarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva. Of the Vatsa sagotra, the gotrajā is Jñānajā, with five pravaras: Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni. Of the Vātsa sagotra, the gotrajā is Jñānajā, with five pravaras: Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni. Of the Vātsya sagotra, the gotrajā is Śīharī, with five pravaras: Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni. Of the Śyāmāyana sagotra, the gotrajā is Śīharī, with the pravara: Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni. Of the Dhāraṇa sagotra, the gotrajā is Chatrajā, with three pravaras: Agastya, Dārvacyuta, and Dadhyavāhana. Of the Kāśyapa gotra, the gotrajā is Cāmuṇḍā, with three pravaras: Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, and Naidhruva. Of the Bharadvāja gotra, the gotrajā is Pakṣiṇī, with three pravaras: Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja. Of the Māṇḍavya sagotra, Vatsa, Vātsya, and Vātsyāyana, the four share common [ancestry]. Of the Laugākṣa sagotra, the gotrajā is Bhadrayoginī, with three pravaras: Kāśyapa, Vasiṣṭha, and Avatsāra. Of the Kauśika sagotra, the gotrajā is Pakṣiṇī, with three pravaras: Viśvāmitra, Atharva, and Bhāradvāja. The common pravara is one: Paiṅgya and Bharadvāja share the same pravaras. Laugākṣa, Gārgyāyaṇa, and the Kāśyapas—these four share common pravaras. Kauśika and Kuśika—these two share a common pravara. Aupamanyava and Laugākṣa—these two share common pravaras.
For as many as in whose pravaras Viśvāmitra alone recurs,
Because of having the same gotra, marriage must not take place among so many with one another. (5)

Among five [ancestral seers], non-marriage applies when three are common; among three, when two are common. (8ab)
This is so in the groups of the Bhṛgus and Aṅgirases; in the rest, even a single [common ancestor] prohibits [marriage]. (8cd)
If one marries a maiden of the same gotra and pravara and approaches her, (9ab)
and fathers a cāṇḍāla on her, he falls from his very status as a brahmin. (9cd)
Kātyāyana says: (10a)
Having married [a maiden] of the same gotra, and likewise of the same pravara, (11a)
the twice-born man, after abandoning her, should perform the cāndrāyaṇa penance. (10b/12)
Having forsaken that wife, he should thereafter protect her like a mother. (11cd)
Yājñavalkya says: (14a)
[One should marry a woman] free from disease, who has brothers, not born of the same ṛṣi or gotra, (15ab)
beyond the fifth [degree] on the mother's side and the seventh on the father's side. (12/16)
“Marriage is with those not having the same pravara,” so says Gautama. (17a)
Even if one pravara is different for the groom [relative to] the mother's gotra, (18ab)

and bowing with hymns fittingly, the sages spoke to Mārkaṇḍa:

Nārada said:
O Blessed One, Lord of the gods of gods, cause of creation and dissolution,
transcending the guṇas, endowed with guṇas, supreme means to liberations,
having established the mansion of the Vedas and the excellent brahmins according to rule,
what then did the lord of the Raghus do after going back to Ayodhyā?
What duties did the brahmins perform there in their own abode?
Brahmā said:
Devoted to sacrifices and charitable works, tranquil, averse to accepting gifts,
they ruled this forest. The royal priest, best of brahmins,
spoke the supreme māhātmya of sacred fords before Rāma:
the māhātmya of Prayāga and the supreme fruit of the Triveṇī,
the greatness of Prayāga sacred ford and indeed of Śuklatīrtha,
likewise the greatness of Siddhakṣetra, Kāśī, and Gaṅgā.
Vasiṣṭha recounted other sacred fords, O Nārada:
of Dharmāraṇya, Suvarṇā, and that sacred field of Hari;
all [acts like] ritual ablution and giving [there] are a barley-corn greater than at Vārāṇasī.
Hearing this, the divine Rāma, his mind astonished,
desiring to make a pilgrimage again to Dharmāraṇya, set out.
Accompanied by Sītā, the knower of righteousness preceded by a large army,
with his brother Lakṣmaṇa, having Bharata as his helper,
surrounded by Śatrughna, he went to the city of Moheraka.

chanting the name of Rāma, the son of Daśaratha, repeatedly saying, 'Rāma, Rāma':
'I am the servant of that servant, both of Rāma and of the twice-born.
Blinded by the darkness of ignorance, I have indeed become blind now.
And I have obtained the collyrium, the great remedy of Rāma’s name.
Indeed, whatever mortals abandon Rāma and worship another deity,
they are burned by fire, O master, just as I, whose mind is foolish, [have been burned].
Hari is the Bhāgīrathī, O brahmins; the brahmins are the Bhāgīrathī [and] Hari.
The Bhāgīrathī, Hari, [and] the brahmins are the single essence in the three worlds.
And the staircase to heaven here consists of the brahmins, the Bhāgīrathī, [and] Hari,
by which one is led to Vaikuṇṭha with the great rope of Rāma's name.'
Thus bowing down with folded hands, the king spoke this word:
'Let the fire be appeased, O brahmins; I grant you a charter.

3.2.m:
I am your servant now, O brahmins; may my word not prove false.
Whatever sin belongs to the murder of a brahmin, to those who violate another’s wife,
whatever sin belongs to drinkers of liquor and likewise to thieves of gold,
whatever sin belongs to slayers of gurus—may that sin be mine [if I fail]!
Whatever desire one thinks of, that very thing I shall grant again.
Devotion to the brahmins must always be practiced, and likewise devotion to Rāma.
Never should anything contrary be done by me, O best of the twice-born!'
Vyāsa said:
On that occasion, the brahmins became compassionate toward the king.
The other small packet which remained was given for the appeasement of the curse.
And when the hairs were cast, that army was restored to life.
The quarters became clear; the sounds arising from the quarters ceased.
The subjects there became at ease, their minds overflowing with joy.
Sons, grandsons, and the rest remained as before.
And the people became obedient to the commands of the brahmins, just as in former times.
Apart from the dharma of Viṣṇu, they recognized no other dharma.

3.2.m:
Having issued a new royal charter according to rule, as before,
the heretics who had propagated fabricated treatises were expelled.
Those who stood outside the Vedas perished—the high, the low, and the middling.
The thirty-six thousand who formerly had been Gobhujas—
among them arose the merchants of Aḍhavīja lineage.
All of them were appointed by the king to the service of the brahmins.
Practicing good conduct, highly skilled, worshippers of gods and brahmins,
having abandoned the heretical path, they were devoted to Viṣṇu.
Approaching the bank of the Jāhnavī, the king granted [gifts] to the masters of the three Vedas.
Indeed, when the charter was given to them with devotion,
those brahmins who had deviated from the duty of their place arrived.
The king was petitioned by those trouble-making brahmins as follows:
'O king, expel those eminent brahmins who have broken their word!'
Mutual disputes arose concerning the granted livelihood.
And the members of the assembly were summoned to administer justice.

3.2.m:
When the signatures were examined, each was proved separately.
Hearing this, the king then indeed performed the gift of one's weight [in gold].
While the gift was being given, the masters of the four Vedas spoke:
'Our caste has been lost by us; how can we accept this gift?'
Then all those twice-born Moherakas were expelled from the place,
fifteen thousand [in number], who had mastered the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences.
Thereupon, O king, by that monarch who followed Rāma,
those brahmins were summoned, and he established a division of castes.
Those brahmins versed in the three Vedas who had gone to the Lord toward Setubandha
should receive the livelihood; the others should have no share in the livelihood.
Those who did not go there attained the status of masters of the four Vedas.
There was to be no connection with merchants, nor marriage with them,
nor any connection in the village livelihood, once the caste division was made.
The Śūdras devoted to serving twice-borns, who were not corrupted by heretics,
and who turned away from the Jaina faith, became excellent landowners.

3.2.m:
And those who were devoted to heresy and broke the royal decree of Rāma,
all those brahmins as well as Śūdras were placed under restraint.
Those who kept true to their vows remained there and were happy.
The Cāturvidyas were made to dwell outside the village by that king,
[thinking,] "I must certainly act in such a way that Rāma is not angered."
Indeed, those who turned their backs on Rāma but followed the virtuous
are to be known as Cāturvidyas; they were then deprived of their livelihood.
Then King Kumārapāla, having accomplished his duty,
spoke words with humility before the brahmins:
"The village livelihood was not abolished by me; indeed, this was ordained by fate.
When men commit offences themselves, to whom should blame not be assigned?
Just as in a forest, fire may arise from the friction of dry wood by the decree of fate,
so was a condition made by you for the sake of a token of recognition.
Having issued the decree of Rāma for the sake of the son of the wind-god,
you brahmins turned away—to whom is that fault to be attributed?
Even if laden with great sin, remembering Hari at the moment of death,

a man quickly goes to the world of Viṣṇu; how could there be any doubt about this?
When great merit arises, men's minds are turned toward the highest good;
and at the time sin arises, it becomes quite the opposite.
He who continually protects these three worlds by means of dharma,
and who is the inner Self of living beings—doubt concerning him is not beneficial.
All the immortals beginning with Indra, and those rich in austerity beginning with Sanaka,
worship here for the sake of liberation—doubt concerning him is not beneficial.
The name of Rāma is sung as equal to the thousand names [of Viṣṇu];
having felt hesitation regarding it, how could accomplishment arise here?
Out of the merit earned throughout my lives, Hari gave me this token of recognition.
Whatever sin was incurred from heresy has been wiped away by bowing to you;
may you be pleased with me, abandoning your anger toward me now."
The brahmins said:
"O king, your virtue was lost, and yet it has been recovered once again.

Let the Traividyas, true to their vows, enjoy the decree of Rāma;
but give us another place where we may dwell."
Hearing their words, wishing for the happiness of the twice-born,
he gave them a place called Sukhavāsa.
Gold, patterned garments, wish-yielding cows, O king,
all kinds of gold ornaments, and a heap of various articles—
having given [all this] with supreme faith, the ruler of men found joy.
Those are to be known as Traividyas who were settled by the three deities;
settled in Sukhavāsa by the fourth, the king,
those excellent twice-born became the Cāturvidyas in the Kali age.
All those Cāturvidyas, established in Dharmāraṇya,
bestowed blessings prescribed by the Vedas upon that great-souled king.
Being carried by chariots and horses, having achieved their purpose,
the twice-born, filled with great joy, reached the great Moheraka.
