3.2.m:
On the thirteenth day of the bright half of Pauṣa, the charter was obtained by the twice-born,
and an offering was made, dedicated to the family deity.
Every year the offering must be made according to ritual prescription,
and an auspicious ritual ablution must be performed by the noble man.
On that day one should certainly arrange song, dance, and instrumental music,
in such a way that on that day in that month, no loss of livelihood may occur.
If, by fate, when the time has passed, an occasion of growth occurs,
then having performed [the rite] first, the growth rite is prescribed afterwards.
The Traividyas of the Moḍha lineage, who are mostly of distinct lineages,
and the Cāturvedins perform the worship of the family deity.
It should be performed within the year, even when Janārdana is asleep.
And if someone neglects it in the month of Pauṣa and performs Vedic and Smārta rituals,
the family deities, overcome with anger, slay him there.
At the time of a wedding festival, and in rituals such as the tying of the muñja girdle,
the moment belongs to Gaṇanātha; from then on, it is auspicious.

3.2.m:
Those brahmins who were banished by King Āma from their charter
went, fifteen thousand in number, to a pleasant dwelling place.
Rama himself formerly gave fifty-five villages;
the merchants living there provided their livelihood:
The Aḍālajā, Māṇḍalīya, Gobhūja, and pure ones—
they provided the livelihood of the brahmins, devoted to the service of Brahmā.
Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, named 'Description of the Brahmins' Obtaining of Charter and Livelihood,' in the Dharmāraṇyamāhātmya of the first part of the Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses.

3.2.m: Brahmā said: / Listen, O son, I shall declare the supreme secret doctrine. / These great twice-born ones, knowers of the Veda, are said to know the four Vedas. / They constantly perform recitation of scripture, the vaṣaṭ utterance, and the svadhā utterance; / they obey Rama's command and are devoted to devotion to Hanumat. / Then once the gods, led by Brahmā and Viṣṇu, came to Brahmā, / wishing to see the brahmins. / Seeing those gods arrived, they moved from their place; / having offered them respectful water and water for the feet, and likewise the honey mixture, / and then worshipped the gods headed by Brahmā, the brahmins / sat here beside Brahmā and recited the Vedas indeed: / the Saṃhitā text, the Pada text, the Krama text, and likewise the Ghana text; / one should recite aloud the Ṛgveda-saṃhitā of verses. / And the singers of Sāmans perform various hymns of praise, / and the ritual instructions, as well as the yājyā and puronuvākyā verses. / The supreme four-syllabled [utterance], and the four-syllabled, / the two-syllabled, and the five-syllabled, and the two-syllabled: / whoever recites this nature of the sacrifice with knowledge / attains the state of Brahman at the end; I tell the absolute truth. / All the twice-born, with one-pointed minds, were devoted to Vedic recitation. / In their courtyards, deer scratch their hair; / the brahmins recite the mother of the Vedas according to rule, / and young fawns eat the darbha grass held in their hands. / Seeing then that hermitage of the householders devoid of hostility, / the gods were exceedingly delighted, and they said to one another: / 'It is the Tretāyuga now; all are devoted to righteousness. / Kali is said to be wicked, but what will that sinful one do?' / Having summoned the knowers of the four Vedas, the three [gods] said: / 'For your livelihood and for that of the knowers of the three Vedas, / we shall grant you a division; let it be observed properly.

3.2.m: The merchants previously declared are thirty-six thousand; / the knowers of the three Vedas are three thousand; fifteen thousand / are declared to be the knowers of the four Vedas, mutually relying on the livelihood. / The knowers of the three Vedas have three shares, and the knowers of the four have four shares. / Having come to the merchants' house daily for the office of family priest, / having divided the share, they received it, arranged by the Lord of deeds. / There is no mutual marriage between the knower of four Vedas and the knower of three Vedas; / the knowers of four Vedas have been declared by me, and likewise the knowers of three Vedas. / The knowers of three Vedas [take] by a three-part share, and the knowers of four by a four-part share; / thus the caste division was arranged by the Lord of deeds. / Those brahmins, having accomplished their purpose, bowed to those best of gods; / having granted the livelihood, the gods then departed to their own abode. / Those twice-born were inhabitants of fifty-five villages; / they are declared as the knowers of the four Vedas, and from then on, the knowers of the three Vedas. / And fifteen are the lineages of the knower of the four Vedas: / Bhāradvāja, and Vatsa, Kauśika, and Kuśa; / Śāṇḍilya, Kaśyapa, Gautama, and Chādana; / Jātūkarṇya, Kuṃta, Vasiṣṭha, and Dhāraṇa; / Ātreya, Māṇḍila, and Laugākṣa after that. / And I will declare the names of their places in due order: / Sītāpūra, the sacred field, and Magoḍī is remembered thus; / Jyeṭhaloja, and after that Śerathā; / Chedetālī, Vanoḍī, and Govyandalī; / Kaṇṭācoṣalī, Koheca, and Candana; / Thalagrāma, Sohaṃ, Hāthañja, Kapaḍavāṇaka; / Vrajanhorī, Vanoḍī, Phīṇā, Vagola, and Dṛṇa; / Thalajā, Cāraṇa, Siddhā, and Bhālajā after that; / Mahovī, Āīyā, Malīā, Godharī, and Āma after that.

3.2.m:
And likewise Vāṭhasuhālī, Māṇajā, and Sānadīyā; / Ānandīyā, Pāṭaḍīa, and after that Ṭīkolīyā; / Gaṃbhī, Dhaṇīā, Mātrā, and Nātamorā as well; / Valolā, Rāṃtyajā, Rūpolā, and Bodhaṇī; / Chatroṭā, Alu, and after this Vāsataḍīā; / Jāṣāsaṇā, Gotīyā, Caraṇīyā, and Dudhīyā; / Hālolā, Vaiholā, Asālā, and Nālāḍā; / Deholo, Sauhāsīyā, and Saṃhālīyā as well: / these fifty villages in proper order were duly granted / to the brahmins by Rāma according to the rules, as their home. / Beyond this I will describe the lineages of each home, / and the ancestral sages according to the rules. / Knowing the tutelary goddess and the ancestral sages, / the home is known, and the twice-born dwelling in that home.

Nārada said:
How does the gotra arise, and how is the family known? / Or how is the goddess known? Tell me that truly.

Brahmā said:
Sītāpura is the first, having two ancestral sages; / Kuśa and Vatsa have been proclaimed to you here. / In Śrīkṣetra, the second, there are three gotras: / Chāndānasa, Vatsa, and Kuśa as the third. / In the third, Mudgala, Kuśa, and Bhāradvāja; / and Śoholī is the fourth, having the ancestral sage Kuśa; / Jyeṣṭhalā is the fifth, proclaimed as Vatsa and Kuśa; / Śreyasthāna is the sixth, Bhāradvāja and Kuśa; / Daṃtālī is the seventh, Bhāradvāja and Kuśa; / know Vaṭasthāna as the eighth, O best of sons; / the gotras there are Kuśa, Kutsa, and Bhāradvāja; / Rājñīpura is the ninth, having the ancestral sage Bhāradvāja;

The gotras in proper order / and the homes have thus been proclaimed by me here in order. / Those called Śītavāḍiyā are Kuśa and Vatsa, / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Dala as the third; / Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya. / Vacārddā, Śeṣā, and Buṭalā are proclaimed as the lineage goddesses. / This is the first gotra. (1) / Śrīkṣetra is declared the second, having two gotras: / Chāndānasa and Vatsa, and two goddesses; / Āṅgirasa, Aṃbarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva; / Bhṛgu, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya; / the goddess is declared to be Bhaṭṭārikā, and the second is Śepalā. / Hear about those born in this family, O best of sages:

(2) / The third is Magoḍoā, having two gotras: / Bhāradvāja and Kutsa, and two goddesses; / Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja, / Viśvāmitra and Devarāta are the three ancestral sages; / Śeṣalā and Budhalā are proclaimed, and likewise Dhāraśānti. / The brahmins born in this village are speakers of truth, / engaged in rites of honoring twice-born men, devoted to various sacrificial rites; / all the twice-born born in this gotra are lords among sages. / This is the third gotra. (3) / The fourth village is Śīholiyā, having two gotras: / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third; / the goddess Cacāī is proclaimed as their lineage goddess. / Those born in this gotra are weak and miserable in mind, / brahmins who speak untruth, greedy, O best of men; / yet these brahmins are skilled in all branches of learning, O best of sages. / This is the fourth home. (4) / Jyeṣṭhalojā is proclaimed as the fifth home; / Vatsaśīyā and Kutsaśīyā are remembered as the two ancestral lines; / […], Yauvanāśva, Bhṛgu, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya; / Cacāī belongs to the Vatsa gotra, and Śāntā was born in the Kutsa gotra. / Through these three and five [ancestors], the twice-born are embodiments of Brahman: / peaceful, self-controlled, virtuous, endowed with wealth and sons, / devoid of Vedic study, yet skilled in all rituals, / handsome, well-behaved, steadfast in all duties, / all devoted to the duty of giving, these twice-born born here give water. / This is the fifth home. (5) / Those born in the villages of Śerathā are endowed with two ancestral sages: / Kuśa and Bhāradvāja, and likewise two goddesses.

Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third; / Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja likewise.
Kamalā and Mahālakṣmī, and the Yakṣiṇī as the second. / Those born in this gotra are wise men devoted to Vedic and Smārta rites,
accustomed to Vedic study, practitioners of austerity, destroyers of foes, / wrathful, greedy, wicked, engaged in sacrificing for themselves and sacrificing for others; / all are devoted to the rites of the Absolute—these brahmins have been described by me.
Thus is the sixth location. (6)
[The brahmins] of Daṃtālīya belong to Bhāradvāja, Kutsa, and Śāyā [gotras] likewise; / Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja as well.
The goddess is stated to be Yakṣiṇī, and Karmalā as the second. / The brahmins born in this gotra are wealthy and auspicious,
endowed with fine clothes and ornaments, devoted to the worship of twice-born [brahmins], / all fond of feeding brahmins, and all devoted to righteousness.
Thus is the seventh location. (7)
Four pravaras are handed down as born in the lineage of Vaḍodrīya: / Kuśa, Kutsa, Vatsa, and Bhāradvāja likewise.
I shall proclaim their pravaras and their gotras in due order: / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third;
Āṅgirasa, Ambarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva as the third; / Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagni likewise;
Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja as well. / Karmalā, Kṣemalā, and Dhārabhaṭṭārikā;
Kṣemalā is stated as the fourth gotra-mother in succession. / Those born in this gotra are ever devoted to the five sacrifices,
greedy and wrathful, and they produce numerous offspring; / intent on ritual baths, gifting, and the like, always possessing conquered senses,
makers of thousands of stepwells, wells, and ponds; / observant of vows, knowledgeable in virtues, yet foolish and devoid of the Veda.
Thus is the eighth location. (8)
In the village named Godaṇīya, two gotras are situated there: / the Vatsa gotra is the first, and the Bhāradvāja is the second.

Bhṛgu, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Purodhasa; / Śīharī is to be known as the first, and Yakṣiṇī as the second.
The brahmins born in this gotra are endowed with wealth and grain, / indignant, devoid of greed, yet full of malice and deceitful,
harmful and lusting for wealth—so they are described by me, O king.
Thus is the ninth location. (9)
In Kaṇṭavāḍīā village are brahmins born of the Kuśa gotra and the Śukla lineage; / I shall declare its pravara; listen, O best of kings:
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala are remembered as the three; / Cacāī is declared as their goddess; listen, O best of kings!
There they sacrifice with rituals, their minds rejoiced and focused; / brahmins skilled in all sciences and speakers of truth.
Thus is the tenth location. (10)
Those born in the Kutsa lineage have been declared by me as Vekhaloyā; / they are endowed with three pravaras; listen, O best of kings:
Viśvāmitra, Devarāja, and Udala are remembered as the three. / Cacāī is remembered as their goddess, the protectress of the family.
Brahmins of great soul, full of purity and endowed with virtue, / ascetics and yogins, mastering the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
virtuous, of good conduct, devoted to devotion to Viṣṇu, / ever intent on ritual bath and twilight worship, devoted to feeding brahmins,
are proclaimed by me in this lineage; listen further beyond this.
Thus is the eleventh location. (11)
Those declared as Dehaloḍīā are endowed with the Kutsa pravaras: / Āṅgirasa, Ambarīṣa, and Yuvanāśva as the third.
The gotra goddess has been proclaimed by me as Śrī-Śeṣadurbalā. / Those born in the Kutsa lineage are of good conduct, speaking the truth,
accustomed to Vedic study, yet looking only for faults in others, / indignant, free from fickleness, yet malicious and deceitful,
harmful, and lusting for wealth—those born of Kutsa.
Thus is the twelfth location. (12)

3.2.m:
In Kohe the brahmins are declared as endowed with three gotras: / Bhāradvāja, Vatsa, and Kuśa as the third.
I shall declare their pravaras in the order of the gotras: / Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagni likewise.
The third is the Kuśa pravara consisting of three pravara-seers: / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third.
Yakṣiṇī is declared as the first, and Śīhurī as the second; / Cacāī is declared as the third, in order of gotra origins.
The wise brahmins born in this gotra are devoted to Vedic and Smārta rites, / accustomed to Vedic study, practitioners of austerity, destroyers of foes,
wrathful, greedy, wicked, engaged in sacrificing for themselves and sacrificing for others; / all devoted to brahmanic rites—these best of twice-born have been described by me.
Thus is the thirteenth location. (13)
Those born in Cāṃdaṇakheḍa originate from the Bhāradvāja [gotra]: / Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja as the third;
and Yakṣiṇī was declared as his goddess by the wise Vyāsa. / Those born as Bhāradvājas are twice-born embodying the Absolute,
tranquil, self-restrained, well-behaved, endowed with wealth and sons; / the best of twice-born in Dharmāraṇya, skilled in ritual sacrifices,
all devoted to devotion to their gurus, they illuminate their own family.
Thus is the fourteenth location. (14)
Those born in Thala village originate from the Bhāradvāja [gotra]: / Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja as the third.
The brahmins born in this gotra are wealthy and auspicious, / endowed with fine clothes and ornaments, devoted to the worship of twice-born [brahmins],
all fond of feeding brahmins, all devoted to righteousness. / The gotra goddess was declared by me, Yakṣiṇī named the Protectress.
Thus is the fifteenth location. (15)
Those born as Moūtrīyā—two gotras are declared there: / Bhāradvāja and Kaśyapa, and two goddesses as well;
Cāmuṇḍā and Yakṣiṇī are declared as the goddesses here.

3.2.m:
Kaśyapa, Avatsāra, and Naidhruva as the third; / Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja as the third. / Speaking pleasantly, very capable, ever devoted to service of the guru, / always endowed with prestige, devoted to the welfare of all beings, / those twice-born belonging to Kaśyapa perform great sacrifices. / Conducting sacrifices for all, they are considered supreme sacrificers.
Thus ends the sixteenth settlement. 16.

And those born in Hāthījaṇa are Vatsas and Bhāradvājas. / Jñānajā and Yakṣiṇī are proclaimed as the two lineage deities.
And those born in this lineage are ever engaged in the five daily sacrifices, / greedy, wrathful, possessing offspring, and very learned; / devoted to bathing, charity, and the like, intent on devotion to Viṣṇu, / observant of vows, knowledgeable in virtues, ignorant, devoid of the Veda.
Thus ends the seventeenth settlement. 17.

Now, the brahmins originating from Kapaḍvaṇaja are Bhāradvājas and Kuśas. / Yakṣiṇī is declared as the goddess, and Cacāī as the second.
Āṅgirasa and Bārhaspatya, with Bhāradvāja as the third; / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third.
And those born in this lineage speak the truth, keep strict vows, / control their senses, are handsome, eat little, and have pleasant faces; / ever energetic, knowing the Purāṇas, devoted to making great gifts, / free of malice, accompanied by greed, devoted to Vedic study, / far-sighted, possessing great brilliance, and deluded by the Great Illusion.
Thus ends the eighteenth settlement. 18.

Janhorī brahmins are proclaimed as endowed with the Kuśa pravara: / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third; / and Tāraṇī Mahāmāyā is renowned as the lineage goddess. / The brahmins born in this family, O king, are unbearable: / very fierce, large-bodied, tall, very arrogant, / embodied afflictions, dark-complexioned, skilled in all sacred treatises, / eating much, wealthy, capable, free of malice and sin,

Thus ends the nineteenth settlement. 19.

And those born in Vanoḍīya have a group of three lineages: / the two pravaras are Kuśa and Kutsa, and Bhāradvāja as the third; / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third; / Āṅgirasa, Āmbarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva as the third; / and likewise Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja. / Śeṣalā is declared the first, and Śāntā the second; / and the third is Dhāraśānti: these are the lineage deities in order. / Now, those born in this lineage are weak, feeble-minded, / untruthful brahmins, and greedy, O best of kings, / [yet] skilled in all sciences, brahmins most knowledgeable in the absolute.
Thus ends the twentieth settlement. 20.

Kīṇāvācana is the settlement which is the twenty-first. / The eminent brahmins are declared to be Bhāradvājas, auspicious brahmins: / Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja likewise. / And the goddess Yakṣiṇī is proclaimed as the lineage deity. / And the brahmins born in this lineage are wealthy and auspicious, / endowed with fine garments and ornaments, devoted to serving twice-borns, / all dedicated to feeding brahmins, all intent on righteousness.
Thus ends the twenty-first settlement. 21.

And those supreme brahmins born in their own settlement of Goviṃdaṇā: / the Kuśa lineage is declared, with a triplet of pravaras: / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and the Udala pravara. / And Cacāī, the great goddess, is proclaimed as the lineage deity. / And the brahmins born in this lineage know the absolute; / they sacrifice with offerings there, with delighted minds and single-pointed focus, / skilled in all sciences, friendly to brahmins, best knowers of the absolute.
Thus ends the twenty-second settlement. 22.

Dhāraṇa and Saṅkuśa: this pair of lineages. / Agastya, Dārḍhyacyuta, and Rathyavāhana; / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala as the third. / And Chatrajā is declared the goddess, and Thalatā as the second. / Those born in the Dhāraṇa lineage are friendly to brahmins, best knowers of the absolute, / renowned as having three pravaras, full of goodness, endowed with virtues; / and those born in that lineage adhere to righteous deeds, / wealthy, established in knowledge, in austerity, sacrifices, rites, and the like. / This twenty-third settlement is proclaimed for the Moḍhaka community.
Thus ends the twenty-third settlement. 23.

And those brahmins declared from Vāraṇasiddhi, best knowers of knowledge: / the brahmins in this lineage speak the truth, keep strict vows, / control their senses, are handsome, eat little, and have pleasant faces, / ever energetic, knowing the Purāṇas, devoted to making great gifts, / free from malice, free of greed, devoted to Vedic study, / far-sighted, possessing great brilliance, deluded by the Great Illusion. / This is declared the twenty-fourth settlement, regarded as supreme.
Thus ends the twenty-fourth settlement. 24.

And the truthful brahmins originating from Bhāla are proclaimed here: / the Vatsa lineage and Kuśa, a pair of lineages. / I shall declare their pravaras, sets of five and three: / Bhṛgu, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jamadagni likewise; / Āṅgirasa, Āmbarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva as the third. / And Śāntā and Śeṣalā are the pair of goddesses here. / Those born in this family have good conduct and speak truth, / are calm, of varied complexion, destitute, wearing dirty clothes, / proud, prone to greed, and steadfast in the Vedas and treatises. / This is declared the twenty-fifth settlement of the Moḍha community.
Thus ends the twenty-fifth settlement. 25.

3.2.m: And the Mahovīya brahmins, who know Brahman best: / they have indeed only one holy gotra, named Kuśa. // 59 // / [Its pravaras are] Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Audala as the third. / And the goddess Cavāī resides here in the form of a protector. // 3.2.39.160 // / Those born in this gotra speak truth, master their senses, / keep truthful vows, are handsome, eat sparingly, and have auspicious faces; // 61 // / they are compassionate, merciful, and devoted to the welfare of all beings. / The twenty-sixth abode of those who discuss Brahman has thus been declared. // 62 // / They were praised by Rāma and also by his younger brother. // 63 // / Thus ends the twenty-sixth abode. // 26 // / Now I will declare the Tiyāśrīya [place], their own twenty-seventh abode. / The brahmins born in this place have crossed to the farther shore of the Vedas. // 64 // / The Śāṇḍilya gotra here is proclaimed by the best of Vedic scholars. / It is declared to have five pravaras, and Jñānajā is the deity here: // 65 // / Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, Śāṇḍilya, Asita, / and Devala as the fifth are the pravaras in order; / and the goddess Jñānajā is declared to be the deity of the place. // 66 // / The twice-born born in this lineage possess the splendor of the sun; / all of them are cool like the moon, residing in Dharmāraṇya. // 67 // / They observe good conduct, O great king, devoted to the Vedas and scriptures; / they perform sacrifices, have auspicious conduct, and are dedicated to truth and purity. // 68 // / Knowing righteousness, prone to generosity, pure, and eager for joy, / devoted to austerity and study of the Vedas, dedicated to justice and righteousness— / the twenty-seventh abode has been declared by the knowers of Brahman. // 69 // / Thus ends the twenty-seventh abode. // 27 // / And the Godharīya brahmins, who are the best in knowledge: / I shall now declare their three gotras in order: // 3.2.39.170 // / the first is Dhāraṇasa, and Jātūkarṇa is the second; / the third is Kauśika, in regular succession. // 71 // / Those born in the Dhāraṇasa gotra are endowed with three pravaras:

And Ānandīyā is the settlement, with two gotras: / one named Bhāradvāja, and the second Śāṇḍilya. // 94
Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja is the third; / and the goddess here is Cacāī, proclaimed as the gotra-deity. // 95
Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, Śāṇḍilya, and Asita, / and Devala is the fifth—these are the pravaras in order. // 96
And the goddess Jñānajā is declared to be the gotra-deity. / Those born in this gotra are free from greed, pure in mind, // 97
content with whatever comes by chance, brahmins who are the best knowers of Brahman. // 98
Thus ends the thirty-second settlement. // 32
Pāṭaḍīyā is proclaimed as an exalted, sacred settlement; / here is the Kuśa gotra, endowed with three pravaras: // 99
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala is the third. / Those born in this gotra are devoted to the Vedas and Śāstras; // 100
those brahmins are proud and haughty, promoters of the path of justice. // 1
Thus ends the thirty-third settlement. // 33
Ṭīkoliyā is an exalted settlement, and likewise has the Kuśa gotra: / Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala is the third. // 2
And here the goddess Cacāī is proclaimed as the gotra-deity; / the brahmins born in this gotra are devoted to Śruti and Smṛti, // 3
sickly, greedy, wicked, engaged in sacrificing and conducting sacrifices; / all are intent on rites of Brahman—these are described by me here as Moḍhas. // 4
Thus ends the thirty-fourth settlement. // 34
Gamīdhāṇīya is declared as the supreme thirty-fifth settlement, / where the gotra is Dhāraṇasa, and the goddess here is Mahābalā. // 5
[The pravaras are] Agasti, Dāḍhacyuta, and Idhmavāhana. / The brahmins born in this lineage are devoted to Brahman, // 6
free from greed, very wise, and observers of the commands of the Vedas. // 7
Thus ends the thirty-fifth settlement. // 35
And Mātrā is a supreme settlement, sacred to all embodied beings; / the sacred, supreme Kuśa gotra resides here. // 8

The brahmins born in this lineage are devoted to the gods, / reciting the Svādhyāya and the Vaṣaṭ-call, promoters of the Vedas and Śāstras. // 10
Thus ends the thirty-sixth settlement. // 36
Nātamorā is an exalted settlement, pure, supreme, and auspicious; / and there is the Kuśa gotra, endowed with three pravaras: // 11
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Udala is the third; / and here the goddess Jñānajā is proclaimed as the gotra-deity. // 12
Those born in this lineage are brahmins, the best knowers of Brahman, / knowers of dharma, speakers of truth, devoted to vows and gifts. // 13
Thus ends the thirty-seventh settlement. // 37
And Balolā is a great settlement, sacred and exceedingly wonderful; / the Kuśa gotra is declared, with three pravaras. // 14
The pravaras are as stated before, and the goddess here is Mānadā; / in this lineage, those created by Kājeśa are declared to be excellent. // 15
O best of kings, the brahmins are speakers of untruth and greedy, / [yet] skilled in all sciences, brahmins who are the best among the knowers of Brahman. // 16
Thus ends the thirty-eighth settlement. // 38
And Rājyajā is a great settlement, having the Laugākṣa pravara, / and the three pravaras are Kāśyapa, Avatsāra, and Vāsiṣṭha. // 17
Bhadrā and Yoginī are proclaimed as the gotra-deities; / the brahmins born in this lineage are devoted to the Vedas, // 18
devoted to daily ritual ablution, daily fire-offerings, and daily gift-giving, / engaged in eternal dharma, and intent on daily and occasional duties. // 19
Thus ends the thirty-ninth settlement. // 39
Rūpolā is a supreme settlement, pure and granting great merit; / in it are three gotras and three goddesses. // 20
The first are named Kutsa and Vatsa, and Bhāradvāja is the third; / [the pravaras are] Āṅgirasa, Ambarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva is the third; // 21
[and] Bhṛgu, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya;

The goddess is Kṣemalā, and also Dhārabhaṭṭārikā; / the third gotra mother is declared to be Kṣemalā in order. // 23
Those born in this gotra are always devoted to the five sacrifices; / they are greedy, wrathful, and produce many offspring; // 24

Thus ends the forty-first settlement. // 41
And Chatroṭā is an exalted settlement, worshipped by all the world; / the Kuśa gotra is declared, with three pravaras: // 30
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and the third is Dala; / and the goddess here is Cacāī, proclaimed as the gotra-deity. // 31
Those born in this lineage are devoted to the Vedas and Śāstras; / those brahmins are very prosperous, promoters of the path of justice. // 32
Thus ends the forty-second settlement. // 42
Khala is the settlement here, the forty-third; / the brahmins born of the Vatsa gotra are promoters of agriculture. // 33
The gotra goddess is Jñānajā, and the pravaras are five: / Bhārgava, Cyavana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya. // 34
The brahmins born in this gotra faithfully attend to the Śrauta fires, / are accustomed to Vedic study, ascetics, destroyers of foes, // 35
irritable, greedy, cheerful, engaged in sacrificing and conducting sacrifices.

3.2.m:
Filled with compassion for all beings, and benefactors of others.
Thus ends the forty-third locality. (43)
In Vāsaṃtaḍī, the Kuśa gotra of the vipras is proclaimed.
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Audala indeed is the third.
And Cacāī here is proclaimed as the goddess of the gotra.
And those born in this lineage, as previously stated, are devoted to Brahman,
Benefactors of others, conforming to the minds of others,
Averse to the property of others, and promoters of the supreme path.
Thus ends the forty-fourth locality. (44)
Beyond this, the locality Jākhāsaṇa is proclaimed.
The gotra is named Vātsya, and the goddess born in the gotra is Śīhurī;
And five pravaras have been revealed to you by me:
Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Purodhas are recalled.
And those born in this lineage are brahmins living happily,
Stout vipras, wise, and devoted to all rituals;
All with singular faith in dharma, venerated alone by all the world,
Skilled in the meaning of the Vedas and treatises, devoted to sacrificing and officiating at sacrifices,
Of good conduct, handsome, corpulent, and far-sighted.
And Śīhurī here is proclaimed as the family goddess.
Thus ends the forty-fifth locality. (45)
The forty-sixth locality is revealed as that of the Moṭās;
It is known by the name of Gotī, and here lies the Kuśa gotra.
Viśvāmitra is the first, Devarāta is the second,
And Audala is the third: these are the three pravaras.
And the goddess here is Yakṣiṇī, the destroyer of rākṣasas.
Those brahmins born in this lineage are devoted to Brahman,
With their minds turned toward dharma, and steadfast in the dharmaśāstras.
Thus ends the forty-sixth locality. (46)
And the forty-seventh locality is proclaimed,
The locality named Varalīya, considered supremely sacred.
Likewise is the Bhāradvāja gotra, and likewise the pravaras:

And Yakṣiṇī here is proclaimed as the family goddess.
Āṅgirasa, Bārhaspatya, and Bhāradvāja the third.
And the brahmins born in this lineage are of purified forms,
By the mere water of whose words sinful men are purified.
Thus ends the forty-seventh locality. (47)
The supreme locality named Dudhī has two gotras:
The Dhāraṇa gotra and the Āṅgirasa gotra.
Named Agasti, Dāḍhacyuta, and Idhmavāhana;
And the great goddess Chatrāī; hear the second pravara:
Āṅgirasa, Aṃbarīṣa, and Yauvanāśva the third.
Jñānadā and Śeṣalā—the giver of knowledge to all embodied beings.
O king, the brahmins born in this lineage are irresistible,
Fierce with pride, large-bodied, tall, and arrogant with power,
Arousing distress, dark-complexioned, skilled in all weapons,
Great eaters, wealthy, capable, and free from malice and sin.
Thus ends the forty-eighth locality. (48)
I shall proclaim Hāsolāsa, celebrated as a proper locality here.
Here is the Śāṇḍilya gotra, endowed with five pravaras:
Bhārgava, Cyāvana, Āpnavāna, Aurva, and Jāmadagnya.
And the goddess here is Yakṣiṇī, pure and destroying sin.
And the brahmins born in this lineage are stout-bodied,
Pot-bellied, long-eared, long-armed, great twice-borns,
Free from disease, ever godlike, and devoted to vows of truth.
Thus ends the forty-ninth locality. (49)
And the locality named Vaihāla is indeed the fiftieth.
Likewise is the Kuśa gotra, and the goddess here is Mahābalā.
The vipras born in this gotra are wicked, crooked in their ways,
Wealthy, steadfast in dharma, having mastered the Vedas and Vedāṅgas,
All devoted to gifts and enjoyment, and with their minds set on Vedic rites.
Thus ends the fiftieth locality. (50)

Kuśa and Dhāraṇa, and the pravaras in order:
Viśvāmitra, Devarāta, and Devala the third.
And the goddess Jñānajā is proclaimed as the gotra goddess.
Thus ends the fifty-first locality. (51)
Nālolā is the supreme locality, indeed the fifty-second.
Vatsagotra is thus renowned, and the second is Dhāraṇa.
The pravaras are as previously spoken, and the goddess was spoken of previously indeed.
And those born in this lineage are regarded as supreme and pure.

All are pure, great-souled, and all possess an unbroken lineage.
Thus ends the fifty-second locality. (52)
Dehola is the supreme locality of brahmins, O scorcher of foes;
Born there are the vipras sprung from the Kuśa lineage, O best of men.
The pravaras are indeed those previously spoken, and the goddess was mentioned by me previously.
The twice-born born in that gotra are endowed with the qualities previously stated.
Thus ends the fifty-third locality. (53)
The locality Sohāsīyāpura has three gotras:
It is celebrated as Bhāradvāja, and likewise the gotra Vatsa.
Yakṣiṇī, Jñānajā, and Siholī in order;
And the assessment of these lineages has been spoken previously, O best of kings.
Thus ends the fifty-fourth locality. (54)
Now I will proclaim to you the fifty-fifth locality:
The locality named Saṃhāliyā, given formerly by Rāma.
There indeed dwell brahmins of the Kutsa gotra, endowed with Vedic splendor,

Lolāsaṇā the fifteenth, and likewise Vārolā the sixteenth;
And Nāgalapurā is stated by me here as the seventeenth.
Brahmā said:
As for those Cāturvidya brahmins who, having not arrived [at first], came later,
those best of the twice-born made their dwelling in that delightful place.
Twenty-four in number, desiring the grant issued by Rāma,
they went to Hanumat and, turning back, came again.
Through their fault, all of them incurred displacement from their abodes.
When some time had elapsed, conflict arose among them.
They had divergent customs, divergent speech, and became questionable in their attire.
Whatever brahmins were among those fifteen thousand,
some became devoted to the work of farming, while some were intent on Vedic sacrifice;
some became wrestlers, and some were reciters of the Veda;
some were devoted to Āyurveda, and some were priests to washermen;
some were devoted to the twilight ritual ablutions, while some were priests to indigo-dyers;
some were intent on begging from weavers, seeking alms from cloth-makers and the like.
When the Kali age arrives, the twice-born will become fallen; of this there is no doubt.

3.2.m:
Division of castes will occur among the śūdras when the Kali age arrives, O ruler of men.
Knowing them to be fallen in conduct, afflicted by the bonds of their kin,
they were abandoned in food and clothing, O king, by their own people.
No one would ever marry a maiden to them due to contact [with them].
Then they became merchants, O king, and oil-pressers indeed in the Kali age;
some were distillers, and some prepared husked grain;
some took refuge with princes, and some took refuge with various castes.
When the Kali age arrived, some merchants on the surface of the earth fell indeed.
Their customs became separate, and their connections were severed.
And the dwelling of some came to be in Sītāpura.
Some settled here and there on the bank of the Sābharmatī.
Those who previously came terrified from Sītāpura,
who had settled in the sacred field on the northern bank of the Sābharmatī—
when their place and abode of pleasant habitation was granted,
they themselves immediately went again to that Sītāpura.

And fifty-five villages were given upon their return
by Rāma for the Moḍha brahmins, and they made their dwellings in them.
Those brahmins who were excluded from livelihood, staying within Dharmāraṇya, [said:]
‘We have no interest in the livelihood of merchants, nor any in a village livelihood;
we have no need of that, O best of brahmins, but dwelling here pleases us.’
When this was said, permitted by those Traividya best of the twice-born,
those brahmins, Cāturvidya best of the twice-born, [settled] in those villages.
Devoted to their own duties, peaceful, and intent on the work of farming,
they pastured cattle not far from Dharmāraṇya.
Many boys of the twice-born became cowherds there;
the Cāturvidya youths pastured their cows.
To provide meals for them, young women, widows,
and children brought hospitable food, drink, and the like.
In some course of time, O king, mutual affection arose among them;
the cowherds passionately enjoyed the maidens, daughters of the twice-born.
They all became pregnant; seen by those best of the twice-born,

Considering that this had been obtained, those twice-born, filled with greed,
and those who had gone to the great seat were filled with astonishment.
In their midst, a certain brahmin spoke to them in anger:
The brahmin said:
Indeed they speak untruth, overcome by great greed,
exceedingly greedy for a brahmin's property, leading to the destruction of their sons and grandsons!
They say poison is not real poison; a brahmin's property is called poison.
Poison kills a single person, but a brahmin's property kills sons and grandsons.
When sons, wives, houses, and the rest are consumed by a brahmin's property,
even those who are destroyed by a brahmin's property do not endure.
One who constantly steals a brahmin's property never attains heaven.
Whenever people steal even a cowrie belonging to a brahmin,
the thief must go to hell for three lifetimes.
The ancestors never enjoy the water offered by him;
on the day of their death-rite they do not enjoy his rites of rice-balls and water.

The eleven brahmins said:
O brahmins, an untruth has not been spoken; why do you blame us?
Without a fault, whose harsh speech is ever warranted?
Hearing that, O Pārtha, the merchant who collected from the village
was questioned by those twice-born, and he related the whole reason:
“Tribute was indeed given to me by the merchants, O best of the twice-born.”
Everything was told with an honest heart to the twice-born.
Then, knowing the faction of half [the share], those sons of brahmins grew enraged.
Those eleven twice-born were thereupon cast out from their livelihood.
A caste known as the Ekādaśasama became famous in the three worlds.
No social relation with them occurs, nor does any marriage.
Those who belong to the Ekādaśasama dwell outside the village.
In this way divisions arose among the various Moḍha twice-born,
in the course of time according to the yuga, in respect of castes or righteousness.

धर्मारण्ये महातीर्थे सर्वे ते द्विजसेवकाः ..
अभवन्रामभक्ताश्च रामाज्ञां पालयंति च .. 3.2.40.50 ..
3.2.m: In the great sacred ford of Dharmāraṇya, they were all servants of the twice-born; / they were devotees of Rāma, and they obey Rāma's command.

3.2.s:
ājñāmatyā''dareṇeha hanūmaṃtaśca vīryavān ..
pālayetso'pi cedānīṃ suprāpte vai kalau yuge .. 51 .
3.2.d:
आज्ञामत्या'ऽदरेणेह हनूमंतश्च वीर्यवान् ..
पालयेत्सोऽपि चेदानीं सुप्राप्ते वै कलौ युगे .. 51 .
3.2.m: The valorous Hanūmat also with great reverence / protects that command even now, when the Kali age has properly arrived.

3.2.s:
adṛṣṭarūpī hanumāṃstatra bhramati nityaśaḥ..
traividyā vāḍavā yatra cāturvidyāstathaiva ca .. 52 ..
3.2.d:
अदृष्टरूपी हनुमांस्तत्र भ्रमति नित्यशः..
त्रैविद्या वाडवा यत्र चातुर्विद्यास्तथैव च .. 52 ..
3.2.m: In an unseen form, Hanumān constantly wanders there / where the brahmins knowing three Vedas and knowing four Vedas reside.

3.2.s:
sabhāyāmupaviṣṭā ye'nyāyātpāpaṃ prakurvate ..
jayo hi nyāyakartṝṇāmajayo'nyāyakāriṇām .. 53 ..
3.2.d:
सभायामुपविष्टा येऽन्यायात्पापं प्रकुर्वते ..
जयो हि न्यायकर्तॄणामजयोऽन्यायकारिणाम् .. 53 ..
3.2.m: For those seated in the assembly who commit sin through injustice: / victory belongs to those who act righteously, and defeat to those who act unjustly.

3.2.s:
sāparādhe yastu putre tāte bhrātari cāpi vā ..
pakṣapātaṃ prakurvīta tasya kupyati vāyujaḥ.. 54..
3.2.d:
सापराधे यस्तु पुत्रे ताते भ्रातरि चापि वा ..
पक्षपातं प्रकुर्वीत तस्य कुप्यति वायुजः.. 54..
3.2.m: If someone shows partiality towards a son, father, or brother / who has committed an offense, the son of the Wind becomes angry with him.

3.2.s:
kupito hanumāneṣa dhananāśaṃ karoti vai..
putranāśaṃ karotyeva dhāmanāśaṃ tathaiva ca .. 55 ..
3.2.d:
कुपितो हनुमानेष धननाशं करोति वै..
पुत्रनाशं करोत्येव धामनाशं तथैव च .. 55 ..
3.2.m: Enraged, this Hanumān brings about the loss of wealth, / he brings about the loss of sons, and likewise the loss of home.

3.2.s:
sevārthaṃ nirmitaḥ śūdro na viprānpariṣevate ..
vṛttiṃ vā na dadātyeva hanumāṃstasya kupyati .. 56 ..
3.2.d:
सेवार्थं निर्मितः शूद्रो न विप्रान्परिषेवते ..
वृत्तिं वा न ददात्येव हनुमांस्तस्य कुप्यति .. 56 ..
3.2.m: If a Śūdra, created for the purpose of service, does not serve the brahmins / or does not give their livelihood, Hanumān becomes angry with him.

3.2.s:
arthanāśaṃ putranāśaṃ sthānanāśaṃ mahā bhayam ..
kurute vāyuputro hi rāmavākyamanusmaran .. 57..
3.2.d:
अर्थनाशं पुत्रनाशं स्थाननाशं महा भयम् ..
कुरुते वायुपुत्रो हि रामवाक्यमनुस्मरन् .. 57..
3.2.m: Remembering Rāma’s word, the son of the Wind brings about / loss of wealth, loss of sons, loss of dwelling, and great fear.

3.2.s:
yatra kutra sthitā viprāḥ śūdrā vā nṛpasattama ..
na nirddhanā bhaveyuste prasādādrāghavasya ca ..58..
3.2.d:
यत्र कुत्र स्थिता विप्राः शूद्रा वा नृपसत्तम ..
न निर्द्धना भवेयुस्ते प्रसादाद्राघवस्य च ..58..
3.2.m: Wherever the brahmins or Śūdras dwell, O best of kings, / they will not become impoverished, by the grace of Rāghava.

3.2.s:
yo mūḍhaścāpyadharmātmā pāpapāṣaṃḍamāśritaḥ .
nijānviprānparityajya parajñātīṃśca manyate .. 59..
3.2.d:
यो मूढश्चाप्यधर्मात्मा पापपाषंडमाश्रितः .
निजान्विप्रान्परित्यज्य परज्ञातींश्च मन्यते .. 59..
3.2.m: That fool, unrighteous in mind, who resorts to sinful heresy, / and, abandoning his own brahmins, honors the kinfolk of others,

3.2.s:
tasya pūrvakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ bhasmībhavati nānyathā ..
anyeṣāṃ dīyate dānaṃ svalpaṃ vā yadi vā bahu .. 3.2.40.60 ..
3.2.d:
तस्य पूर्वकृतं पुण्यं भस्मीभवति नान्यथा ..
अन्येषां दीयते दानं स्वल्पं वा यदि वा बहु .. 3.2.40.60 ..
3.2.m: the religious merit he acquired previously turns to ash; it cannot be otherwise. / When a gift is given to others, whether small or great,

3.2.s:
yathā bhavati vai pūrvaṃ brahmaviṣṇuśivaiḥ kṛtam ..
tasya devā na gṛhṇaṃti hṛvyaṃ kavyaṃ ca pūrvajāḥ .. 61..
3.2.d:
यथा भवति वै पूर्वं ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवैः कृतम् ..
तस्य देवा न गृह्णंति हृव्यं कव्यं च पूर्वजाः .. 61..
3.2.m: just as it was anciently ordained by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva, / the gods do not accept his offering to the gods, nor the ancestors his offering to the ancestors.

3.2.s:
vaṃcayitvā nijānviprānanyebhyaḥ pradadettu yaḥ ..
tasya janmārjitaṃ puṇyaṃ bhasmībhavati tatkṣaṇāt ..62..
3.2.d:
वंचयित्वा निजान्विप्रानन्येभ्यः प्रददेत्तु यः ..
तस्य जन्मार्जितं पुण्यं भस्मीभवति तत्क्षणात् ..62..
3.2.m: He who defrauds his own brahmins and gives to others instead, / the religious merit earned across his lifetimes turns to ash that very moment.

3.2.s:
brahmaviṣṇuśivaiścaiva pūjitā ye dvijottamāḥ.. te
ṣāṃ ye vimukhāḥ śūdrā raurave nivasaṃti te.. 63..
yo laulyācca kulācāraṃ gotrācāraṃ pralopayet..
svācāraṃ yo na kurvīta kadācidvai vimohitaḥ..64..
sarvanāśo bhavettasya bhasmībhavati tatkṣaṇāt ..
tasmātsarvaḥ kulācāraḥ sthānācārastathaiva ca .. 65..
3.2.d:
ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवैश्चैव पूजिता ये द्विजोत्तमाः.. ते
षां ये विमुखाः शूद्रा रौरवे निवसंति ते.. 63..
यो लौल्याच्च कुलाचारं गोत्राचारं प्रलोपयेत्..
स्वाचारं यो न कुर्वीत कदाचिद्वै विमोहितः..64..
सर्वनाशो भवेत्तस्य भस्मीभवति तत्क्षणात् ..
तस्मात्सर्वः कुलाचारः स्थानाचारस्तथैव च .. 65..
3.2.m: Those excellent twice-born honored by Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva— / the Śūdras who turn away from them dwell in Raurava. / He who, out of greed, would abolish his family customs or lineage customs, / or who, thoroughly deluded, would ever fail to perform his own proper duties, / suffers complete ruin; it turns to ash that very moment. / Therefore, every family custom and local custom as well,

3.2.s:
gotrācāraḥ pālanīyo yathāvittānusārataḥ ..
evaṃ te kathitaṃ rājandharmāraṇyaṃ purātanam.. 66..
3.2.d:
गोत्राचारः पालनीयो यथावित्तानुसारतः ..
एवं ते कथितं राजन्धर्मारण्यं पुरातनम्.. 66..
3.2.m: and lineage custom must be maintained according to one's wealth. / Thus has the ancient Dharmāraṇya been related to you, O king,

3.2.s:
sthāpitaṃ devadevaiśca brahmaviṣṇuśivādibhiḥ ..
dharmāraṇyaṃ kṛtayuge tretāyāṃ satyamaṃdiram..
dvāpare vedabhavanaṃ kālau moherakaṃ smṛtam .. 67 . . !
brahmovāca .. ..
ya idaṃ śṛṇuyātputra śraddhayā parayā yutaḥ..
dharmāraṇyasya māhātmyaṃ sarvakilbiṣanāśanam .. 68..
3.2.d:
स्थापितं देवदेवैश्च ब्रह्मविष्णुशिवादिभिः ..
धर्मारण्यं कृतयुगे त्रेतायां सत्यमंदिरम्..
द्वापरे वेदभवनं कालौ मोहेरकं स्मृतम् .. 67 . . !
ब्रह्मोवाच .. ..
य इदं शृणुयात्पुत्र श्रद्धया परया युतः..
धर्मारण्यस्य माहात्म्यं सर्वकिल्बिषनाशनम् .. 68..
3.2.m: established by the gods of gods: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, and the rest. / It is called Dharmāraṇya in the Kṛta age, Satyamandira in the Tretā, / Vedabhavana in the Dvāpara, and Moheraka in the Kali age. / Brahmā said: / Whoever hears this with supreme faith, my son, / this māhātmya of Dharmāraṇya, which destroys all sins,

3.2.s:
manovākkāyajanitaṃ pātakaṃ trividhaṃ ca yat..
tatsarvaṃ nāśamāyāti śravaṇātkīrtanātsukṛt .. 69..
3.2.d:
मनोवाक्कायजनितं पातकं त्रिविधं च यत्..
तत्सर्वं नाशमायाति श्रवणात्कीर्तनात्सुकृत् .. 69..
3.2.m: whatever threefold sin was born of mind, speech, or body, / all of it is destroyed by hearing or reciting [it] well.

3.2.s:
dhanyaṃ yaśasyamāyuṣyaṃ sukhasaṃtānadāyakam..
māhātmyaṃ śṛṇuyādvatsa sarvasaukhyāptaye naraḥ .. 3.2.40.70 ..
3.2.d:
धन्यं यशस्यमायुष्यं सुखसंतानदायकम्..
माहात्म्यं शृणुयाद्वत्स सर्वसौख्याप्तये नरः .. 3.2.40.70 ..
3.2.m: Bestowing fortune, fame, longevity, happiness, and offspring, / a man should hear this māhātmya, my child, to obtain all happiness.

3.2.s:
sarvatīrtheṣu yatpuṇyaṃ sarvakṣetreṣu yatphalam..
tatphalaṃ samavāpnoti dharmāraṇyasya sevanāt .. 71 ..
3.2.d:
सर्वतीर्थेषु यत्पुण्यं सर्वक्षेत्रेषु यत्फलम्..
तत्फलं समवाप्नोति धर्मारण्यस्य सेवनात् .. 71 ..
3.2.m: Whatever religious merit is in all sacred fords, whatever fruit in all sacred fields, / that fruit he obtains completely from serving Dharmāraṇya.

3.2.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
dharmāraṇyasya māhātmyaṃ yacchrutaṃ tvanmukhāṃbujāt ..
dharmavāpyāṃ yatra dharmmastapastepe suduṣkuram .. 72..
3.2.d:
.. नारद उवाच .. ..
धर्मारण्यस्य माहात्म्यं यच्छ्रुतं त्वन्मुखांबुजात् ..
धर्मवाप्यां यत्र धर्म्मस्तपस्तेपे सुदुष्कुरम् .. 72..
3.2.m: Nārada said: / The māhātmya of Dharmāraṇya which has been heard from your lotus face, / where Dharma performed very severe austerity at the Dharmavāpī—

3.2.s:
tasya kṣetrasya mahimā mayā tvatto'vadhāritaḥ ..
svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi dharmāraṇyadidṛkṣayā ..73..
tatra vākyajalaughena pāvito'haṃ caturmukha .. 74 . .
vyāsa uvāca .. ..
idamākhyānakaṃ sarvaṃ kathitaṃ pāṃḍunaṃdana ..
yacchrutvā gosahasrasya phalaṃ prāpnoti mānavaḥ .. ..75..
3.2.d:
तस्य क्षेत्रस्य महिमा मया त्वत्तोऽवधारितः ..
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि धर्मारण्यदिदृक्षया ..73..
तत्र वाक्यजलौघेन पावितोऽहं चतुर्मुख .. 74 . .
व्यास उवाच .. ..
इदमाख्यानकं सर्वं कथितं पांडुनंदन ..
यच्छ्रुत्वा गोसहस्रस्य फलं प्राप्नोति मानवः .. ..75..
3.2.m: the greatness of that sacred field has been comprehended by me from you. / May it be well with you; I shall go, desiring to see Dharmāraṇya. / There I have been purified by the flood of water that is your speech, O Four-faced One! / Vyāsa said: / All this narrative has been related, O son of Pāṇḍu; / hearing which, a man obtains the fruit of [gifting] a thousand cows.

3.2.s:
aputro labhate putrānnirddhano dhanavānbhavet ..
rogī rogātpramucyeta baddho mucyeta baṃdhanāt .. 76 ..
3.2.d:
अपुत्रो लभते पुत्रान्निर्द्धनो धनवान्भवेत् ..
रोगी रोगात्प्रमुच्येत बद्धो मुच्येत बंधनात् .. 76 ..
3.2.m: The childless obtains sons; the penniless becomes wealthy; / the sick is freed from sickness; the bound is released from bondage.

3.2.s:
vidyārthī labhate vidyāmuttamāṃ karmasādhanām ..
tīrthayātrāphalaṃ tasya koṭikanyāphalaṃ labhet .. 77 ..
3.2.d:
विद्यार्थी लभते विद्यामुत्तमां कर्मसाधनाम् ..
तीर्थयात्राफलं तस्य कोटिकन्याफलं लभेत् .. 77 ..
3.2.m: The seeker of learning obtains supreme learning that accomplishes ritual actions; / he obtains the fruit of pilgrimage to sacred fords, the fruit of [gifting] ten million maidens.

3.2.s:
yaḥ śrṛṇoti naro bhaktyā nārī vātha narottama ..
nirayaṃ naiva paśyaṃti ekottaraśataiḥ saha .. 78..
3.2.d:
यः श्रृणोति नरो भक्त्या नारी वाथ नरोत्तम ..
निरयं नैव पश्यंति एकोत्तरशतैः सह .. 78..
3.2.m: Whatever man or woman hears it with devotion, O best of men, / they never see hell, together with one hundred and one [ancestors].

3.2.s:
śubhe deśe niveśyātha kṣaumavastrādibhistathā ..
purāṇapustakaṃ rājanprayataḥ śiṣṭasaṃmataḥ .. 79..
3.2.d:
शुभे देशे निवेश्याथ क्षौमवस्त्रादिभिस्तथा ..
पुराणपुस्तकं राजन्प्रयतः शिष्टसंमतः .. 79..
3.2.m: Then, having placed the Purāṇa manuscript in an auspicious place / upon silken cloth and the like, O king, pure and approved by the virtuous,

3.2.s:
arcayecca yathā nyāyaṃ gaṃdhamālyaiḥ pṛthakpṛthak ..
samāptau nṛpa graṃthasya vācakasyānupūjanam .. 3.2.40.80 ..
3.2.d:
अर्चयेच्च यथा न्यायं गंधमाल्यैः पृथक्पृथक् ..
समाप्तौ नृप ग्रंथस्य वाचकस्यानुपूजनम् .. 3.2.40.80 ..
3.2.m: one should worship it properly with perfumes and garlands individually. / At the conclusion of the book, O king, there is the worship of the reciter

3.2.s:
dānādibhiryathānyāyaṃ saṃpūrṇaphalahetave ..
mudrikāṃ kuṃḍale caiva brahmasūtraṃ hiraṇmayam .. 81 ..
3.2.d:
दानादिभिर्यथान्यायं संपूर्णफलहेतवे ..
मुद्रिकां कुंडले चैव ब्रह्मसूत्रं हिरण्मयम् .. 81 ..
3.2.m: with gifts and the like according to rule, for the sake of obtaining the complete fruit: / a finger-ring, two earrings, and a golden sacred thread,

3.2.s:
vastrāṇi ca vicitrāṇi gaṃdhamālyānulepanaiḥ ..
devavatpūjanaṃ kṛtvā gāṃ ca dadyātpayasvinīm .. 82 ..
3.2.d:
वस्त्राणि च विचित्राणि गंधमाल्यानुलेपनैः ..
देववत्पूजनं कृत्वा गां च दद्यात्पयस्विनीम् .. 82 ..
3.2.m: variegated garments, with perfumes, garlands, and ungents; / having performed worship as to a deity, one should also give a milch cow.

3.2.s:
evaṃ vidhānataḥ śrutvā dharmāraṇyakathānakam..
dharmāraṇyanivāsasya phalamāpnotyasaṃśayam .. 83 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ tṛtīye brahmakhaṇḍe pūrvabhāge dharmāraṇyamāhātmye dharmāraṇyanivāsivyavasthāvarṇanapūrvaka dharmāraṇyapurāṇaśravaṇamāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma catvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 40 ..
3.2.d:
एवं विधानतः श्रुत्वा धर्मारण्यकथानकम्..
धर्मारण्यनिवासस्य फलमाप्नोत्यसंशयम् .. 83 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां तृतीये ब्रह्मखण्डे पूर्वभागे धर्मारण्यमाहात्म्ये धर्मारण्यनिवासिव्यवस्थावर्णनपूर्वक धर्मारण्यपुराणश्रवणमाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम चत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः .. 40 ..
3.2.m:
Having thus heard the narrative of Dharmāraṇya according to the precept, / one undoubtedly obtains the fruit of residing in Dharmāraṇya.
Thus ends the fortieth chapter, named 'The Description of the māhātmya of Hearing the Dharmāraṇya Purāṇa, Preceded by the Description of the Regulations for the Inhabitants of Dharmāraṇya', in the Dharmāraṇyamāhātmya, in the first part of the third Brahmakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa, a compendium of eighty-one thousand [verses]. // 40

.. nārada uvāca .. ..
jñātibhede tu saṃjāte tasminmoherake pure ..
traividyaiḥ kiṃ kṛtaṃ brahmaṃstanmamācakṣva pṛcchataḥ .. 1 ... ..
.. brahmovāca .. ..
svasthāne vāḍavāḥ sarve harṣanirbharamānasāḥ ..
agnihotraparā ke'pi ke'pi yajñaparāyaṇāḥ .. 2 ..
ke'pi cāgnisamādhānāḥ ke'pi smārtā niraṃtaram ..
purāṇanyāyavettāro vedavedāṃgavādinaḥ .. 3 ..
sukhena svānsadācārānkurvanto brahmavādinaḥ ..
evaṃ dharmasamācārānkurvatāṃ kuśalātmanām .. 4 ..
sthānācārānkulācārānadhidevyāśca bhāṣitān ..
dharmaśāstrasthitaṃ sarvaṃ kājeśairuditaṃ ca yat .. 5 ..

3.2.m: Nārada said: / When the division of castes occurred in that town of Moheraka, / what was done by those conversant with the three Vedas, O Brahmā? Relate that to me who am asking. / Brahmā said: / All the brahmins in their own abode, their minds full of joy, / some devoted to the Agnihotra, some intent on Vedic sacrifices, / some tending the sacred fire, some continually engaged in Smārta rites, / knowers of the Purāṇas and Nyāya, expounders of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, / performing their righteous conduct with happiness, speakers of the Veda— / while those skilled souls were thus observing righteous conduct, / the best of brahmins spoke of the traditional duty, / the local customs, the family customs, those spoken by the tutelary goddess, / all that is laid down in the Dharmaśāstras, and that which was proclaimed by the Kājeśas. / The brahmins said: / O brahmins, whoever reveres the document with the red footprints, / he should be known as the chief of the caste; thereafter tribute should be given. / Having prepared red sandalwood, and likewise their renowned family, / with their feet reddened with saffron, anointed with fragrant unguents, flowers, and the like, / uniting, that which is written is called "the Red Footprint". / Attentive, let them all revere the written deed of Rāma; / and let the twice-born always worship the handprint of Rāma. / If there are faults in anyone’s good conduct, such as infidelity and the like, / a punishment should be imposed upon them as properly stated by the twice-born. / Let there be no mark of Rāma’s seal as long as he does not pay the fine; / without paying the fine, the mark of the seal is not to be worn. / And the brahmins should be known as having the seal on their hand, O best of kings. / When a son is born, the father should always give an offering to Śrīmātṛ: / twenty palas of clarified butter and five palas of molasses. / Having worshipped the son with saffron and the like as soon as he is born, / on the sixth day, O king, he should always worship Ṣaṣṭhī. / He should make an offering there with clarified butter and perform a fivefold offering.

3.2.m: He should offer five prastha measures of offerings, accompanied by cloths and coconuts. / Having worshipped the Holy Mother with devotion using saffron and other offerings, / he should not practice deceit in matters of family wealth for the increase of offspring. / That wealth which was borrowed during prosperous times must surely be given back. / Immediately after birth, the natal rite must be performed according to the rule. / And whatever livelihood was specified for the brahmins, that too is divided: / indeed, whatever initial livelihood is obtained, / half of that livelihood should be allocated to the family goddess. / And from a merchant it shall be double when a son is born. / And for the Śūdras of Māṇḍala, this is twelve coins; / for those of Aḍālaja, three times as much; for the Gobhujas, four times as much. / All this has been stated, and similarly for the other Śūdra castes. / When the guilt of homicide arises in a person by the power of fate, / a punishment must be imposed upon him according to rule by those learned in the Veda and Śāstras. / One who speaks unrighteousness in place of righteousness, or casts blame on the blameless, / and one who creates division in the dining-row, is considered equal to the killer of a thousand cows. / The division of livelihood shares, as well as the determination of justice, / must be executed in front of Śrī Rāma’s messenger—this is the decision. / One should perform his worship at that time or always; / one should anoint his body with oil indeed for the pacification of obstacles. / One should offer incense, a lamp, fruit, and various kinds of flowers. / Hanumān, when worshipped, surely grants his desired wish. / For each son, one should perform [rites] before him and nowhere else. / The share for the Holy Mother and Bakulasvāmin should be given first; / afterwards, the acceptance of gifts by the brahmins is to be made—this is settled. / In the assemblies of the brahmins for deciding justice and injustice, / holding the verdict in one's heart, one stationed there should announce it to the twice-born. / Purely through the sense of righteousness, he must avoid bias. / That which is agreed upon by all, and indeed unaltered, is to be enacted.

3.2.m:
If a brahmin summoned there feels fear in the assembly, / his word is not to be heard in setting aside a decided matter. / The person who is ostracized by all the brahmins assembled together / must be avoided by everyone in matters of food, drink, and the like. / No daughter should be given to him, and one who associates with him is deemed the same. / Then a fine should be imposed on him by all the excellent twice-born. / Dining together and the giving of a maiden are prohibited—such is the opinion of the son of Daśaratha. / Whatever sin one commits in order to obtain a place or property, / it dwells in dry and wet food; therefore, one should abandon his food. / One who consumes it becomes a sharer in that sin; his fine shall be according to rule. / He who, though having the power, does not uphold justice, / is to be known as a sharer in sin; this is truth, without a doubt. / He who takes a bribe from sinners who perform wicked deeds, / all their sin falls upon him; of this there is no doubt. / His food is never to be accepted, nor ever his daughter. / A man who seeks the welfare of his sons / should observe all these rules; of this there is no doubt. / Having written this deed, those brahmins rejoiced greatly. / Knowing how, when the terrible Kali age arrives, they might not commit sin, / they all established this righteous law.

Vyāsa said:
When the Kali age arrives, all the twice-born will fall from their places here and there; / they will take sides with partiality and become partisans. / They will feed upon the villages of the mlecchas, destroyed by the Kolas; / those brahmins will fall away from the Veda in the Kali age.
Now begins the Dharmāraṇyakhaṇḍa, the second [section] in the Brahmakhaṇḍa. (3.2)
